# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when the required content genuinely needs more space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via the sync procedure there; re-apply or retire the logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when the required content genuinely needs more space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via the sync procedure there; re-apply or retire the logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

</system-reminder>

2	 * Environment registry: the composition-time inventory of tasks with
3	 * verifiers. Each environment declares a task, its executable checks in the
4	 * completion-standard vocabulary, and whether it is held out for evaluation.
5	 * The registry executes nothing; the
6	 * [trajectory-export Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md)
7	 * owns the design rationale.
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-environments
9	 */

11	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
12	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
13	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
14	// Type-only: the durable event vocabulary this package augments.
15	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
16	import { caseBodiesSha256 } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
17	import type { AuthoredCheck } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
18	import type {
19	  EnvironmentContentHashes,
20	  EnvironmentDefinition,
21	  EnvironmentFilter,
22	  EnvironmentId as EnvironmentIdType,
23	  EnvironmentRunStamp,
24	} from './types.ts'

28	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
29	  interface SessionEventMap {
30	    /**
31	     * Environment run stamp: the environment, its content hashes, the
32	     * repetition, group, and district, the model route, and the declared
33	     * isolation of one run, appended once before the run's first turn.
34	     */
35	    'environment/run': EnvironmentRunStamp
36	  }
37	}

39	/** Self-declared payload version of the `environment/run` event. */
40	export const ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION = 1
41	
42	const ISOLATIONS = new Set(['none', 'process', 'host'])
43	const HEX_64 = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/
44	/** A Windows drive prefix, which no workspace-relative path may carry. */
45	const DRIVE_LETTER = /^[A-Za-z]:/
46	
47	/** SHA-256 hex digest of one UTF-8 string. */
48	function sha256(text: string): string {
49	  return createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('hex')
50	}
51	
52	/**
53	 * Field-ordered tuple of one check, so the inventory digest does not depend on
54	 * the author's object key order. A check without cases digests exactly the
55	 * three fields every check has always carried.
56	 */
57	function checkTuple(check: AuthoredCheck): unknown[] {
58	  const head = [check.id, check.outcome, check.run]
59	  const { cases, caseBodies, treeScope } = check
60	  if (cases === undefined && caseBodies === undefined && treeScope === undefined) return head
61	  return [
62	    ...head,
63	    treeScope ?? null,
64	    cases === undefined ? null : [cases.count, cases.weightTotal, cases.sha256],
65	    caseBodies === undefined ? null : caseBodiesSha256(caseBodies),
66	  ]
67	}
68	
69	/**
70	 * Content hashes of one environment: the prompt, the check inventory in
71	 * authored order (case bodies included), the caller-computed fixture digest,
72	 * and the combined key.
73	 * @param environment - the task and checks to hash.
74	 * @param fixtureSha256 - digest of the fixture files, absent for a task without a fixture.
75	 * @returns the four digests; identical inputs give identical digests.
76	 */
77	export function environmentContentHashes(
78	  environment: Pick<EnvironmentDefinition, 'task' | 'checks'>,
79	  fixtureSha256?: string,
80	): EnvironmentContentHashes {
81	  const promptSha256 = sha256(environment.task.prompt)
82	  const checksSha256 = sha256(JSON.stringify(environment.checks.map(checkTuple)))
83	  const contentSha256 = sha256([promptSha256, fixtureSha256 ?? '', checksSha256].join('\n'))
84	  return { promptSha256, checksSha256, ...fixtureSha256 === undefined ? {} : { fixtureSha256 }, contentSha256 }
85	}
86	
87	function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
88	  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
89	}
90	
91	/** Require one non-empty string field of a durable stamp. */
92	function stampText(value: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {
93	  const field = value[key]
94	  if (typeof field !== 'string' || field === '') throw new Error(`environment/run ${key} must be a non-empty string`)
95	  return field
96	}
97	
98	/** Require one SHA-256 hex field of a durable stamp. */
99	function stampHex(value: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {
100	  const field = stampText(value, key)
101	  if (!HEX_64.test(field)) throw new Error(`environment/run ${key} must be a SHA-256 hex digest`)
102	  return field
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * Decode a value that declares itself as an environment run stamp. Unrelated
107	 * values return `undefined`; a malformed stamp fails replay loudly, as every
108	 * durable payload does at the log boundary.
109	 * @param value - candidate durable payload.
110	 * @returns the validated stamp, or `undefined` for another value kind.
111	 */
112	export function decodeEnvironmentRun(value: unknown): EnvironmentRunStamp | undefined {
113	  if (!isRecord(value) || value['kind'] !== 'environment/run') return undefined
114	  if (value['version'] !== ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION) {
115	    throw new Error(`unsupported environment/run version ${String(value['version'])}`)
116	  }
117	  const heldOut = value['heldOut']
118	  if (typeof heldOut !== 'boolean') throw new Error('environment/run heldOut must be a boolean')
119	  const repetition = value['repetition']
120	  if (typeof repetition !== 'number' || !Number.isSafeInteger(repetition) || repetition < 0) {
121	    throw new Error('environment/run repetition must be a non-negative integer')
122	  }
123	  const model = value['model']
124	  if (!isRecord(model)) throw new Error('environment/run model must be a record')
125	  const isolation = value['isolation']
126	  if (typeof isolation !== 'string' || !ISOLATIONS.has(isolation)) {
127	    throw new Error('environment/run isolation must be none, process, or host')
128	  }
129	  const fixture = value['fixtureSha256'] === undefined ? {} : { fixtureSha256: stampHex(value, 'fixtureSha256') }
130	  const group = value['group'] === undefined ? {} : { group: stampText(value, 'group') }
131	  const district = value['district'] === undefined ? {} : { district: stampText(value, 'district') }
132	  return {
133	    kind: 'environment/run',
134	    version: ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION,
135	    environmentId: EnvironmentId(stampText(value, 'environmentId')),
136	    environmentKind: stampText(value, 'environmentKind'),
137	    heldOut,
138	    promptSha256: stampHex(value, 'promptSha256'),
139	    checksSha256: stampHex(value, 'checksSha256'),
140	    ...fixture,
141	    contentSha256: stampHex(value, 'contentSha256'),
142	    repetition,
143	    ...group,
144	    ...district,
145	    model: { provider: stampText(model, 'provider'), model: stampText(model, 'model') },
146	    isolation: isolation as EnvironmentRunStamp['isolation'],
147	  }
148	}

156	/** Stable error codes for rejected environment registrations. */
157	export type EnvironmentErrorCode =
158	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_ID'
159	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_NO_CHECKS'
160	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_CHECK'
161	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_INVALID_IMMUTABLE'
162	
163	/** Error returned by the environment registry boundary. */
164	export class EnvironmentError extends HarnessError {
165	  /**
166	   * @param message - human-readable rejection reason.
167	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
168	   */
169	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
170	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
171	  constructor(message: string, code: EnvironmentErrorCode) {
172	    super(message, code)
173	  }
174	}

176	/**
177	 * Brand a string as an environment id.
178	 * @param id - raw environment identifier.
179	 * @returns the same string with the compile-time brand.
180	 */
181	export function EnvironmentId(id: string): EnvironmentIdType {
182	  return id as EnvironmentIdType
183	}
184	
185	/** Copy a definition so callers never share the registry's stored check list, case bodies, or immutable set. */
186	function detach(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): EnvironmentDefinition {
187	  const immutable = definition.task.immutable
188	  return {
189	    ...definition,
190	    task: { ...definition.task, ...immutable === undefined ? {} : { immutable: [...immutable] } },
191	    checks: definition.checks.map(check => ({
192	      ...check,
193	      ...check.caseBodies === undefined ? {} : { caseBodies: [...check.caseBodies] },
194	    })),
195	  }
196	}
197	
198	/**
199	 * Reject a declared immutable path the runner could not digest as one workspace
200	 * file or tree: an absolute path, a Windows-style path, a `.` or `..` segment,
201	 * an empty segment, or a repeat. The check-owned set is a security invariant of
202	 * the run, so a path the registry cannot resolve fails registration rather than
203	 * the run that would have measured it.
204	 */
205	function assertImmutable(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): void {
206	  const reject = (path: string, reason: string): never => {
207	    throw new EnvironmentError(
208	      `environment "${definition.id}" declares immutable path "${path}" ${reason}`,
209	      'ENVIRONMENT_INVALID_IMMUTABLE',
210	    )
211	  }
212	  const seen = new Set<string>()
213	  for (const path of definition.task.immutable ?? []) {
214	    if (path === '') reject(path, 'that is empty')
215	    if (path.startsWith('/') || DRIVE_LETTER.test(path)) reject(path, 'that is not workspace-relative')
216	    if (path.includes('\\')) reject(path, 'that uses a backslash; workspace-relative paths separate segments with "/"')
217	    for (const segment of path.split('/')) {
218	      if (segment === '') reject(path, 'that is not normalized: it holds an empty segment')
219	      if (segment === '.' || segment === '..') reject(path, `that is not normalized: it holds a "${segment}" segment`)
220	    }
221	    if (seen.has(path)) reject(path, 'twice')
222	    seen.add(path)
223	  }
224	}
225	
226	/** Reject a definition whose verifiers cannot author a completion standard. */
227	function assertChecks(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): void {
228	  if (definition.checks.length === 0) {
229	    throw new EnvironmentError(`environment "${definition.id}" declares no checks`, 'ENVIRONMENT_NO_CHECKS')
230	  }
231	  const seen = new Set<string>()
232	  for (const check of definition.checks) {
233	    if (seen.has(check.id)) {
234	      throw new EnvironmentError(`environment "${definition.id}" declares check "${check.id}" twice`, 'ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_CHECK')
235	    }
236	    seen.add(check.id)
237	  }
238	}
239	
240	/** Environment registry (`ctx.environments`): tasks with verifiers, held at composition time. */
241	export class EnvironmentRegistry extends Service {
242	  private readonly environments = new Map<EnvironmentIdType, EnvironmentDefinition>()
243	
244	  constructor(ctx: Context) {
245	    super(ctx, 'environments')
246	  }
247	
248	  /**
249	   * Register one environment. Registrations are effects: the producer keeps
250	   * the returned disposer under its own fiber so disposal removes the entry.
251	   * @param definition - complete environment definition.
252	   * @returns the exact disposer that removes this registration and no later one under the same id.
253	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentError} when the id is already registered, the
254	   *   definition declares no checks, two checks share an id, or an immutable
255	   *   path is not a normalized workspace-relative path.
256	   */
257	  register(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): () => void {
258	    if (this.environments.has(definition.id)) {
259	      throw new EnvironmentError(`environment "${definition.id}" is already registered`, 'ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_ID')
260	    }
261	    assertChecks(definition)
262	    assertImmutable(definition)
263	    const stored = detach(definition)
264	    this.environments.set(stored.id, stored)
265	    return () => {
266	      if (this.environments.get(stored.id) === stored) this.environments.delete(stored.id)
267	    }
268	  }
269	
270	  /**
271	   * Read one environment.
272	   * @param id - environment identity.
273	   * @returns a detached definition, or `undefined` when nothing is registered under the id.
274	   */
275	  get(id: EnvironmentIdType): EnvironmentDefinition | undefined {
276	    const stored = this.environments.get(id)
277	    return stored === undefined ? undefined : detach(stored)
278	  }
279	
280	  /**
281	   * List environments in registration order.
282	   * @param filter - kind and held-out selection; absent fields match everything.
283	   * @returns detached definitions.
284	   */
285	  list(filter: EnvironmentFilter = {}): EnvironmentDefinition[] {
286	    return [...this.environments.values()]
287	      .filter(environment => filter.kind === undefined || environment.kind === filter.kind)
288	      .filter(environment => filter.heldOut === undefined || environment.heldOut === filter.heldOut)
289	      .map(detach)
290	  }
291	}
292	
293	export default EnvironmentRegistry

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of the environment domain: identities, the merge-extensible kind
3	 * map, and the task-with-verifiers definition, free of host-side imports.
4	 *
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types
6	 */
7	
8	import type { Branded } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand'
9	import type { AuthoredCheck, CertificateIsolation } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
10	
11	/** Identifies one environment across compositions; derived from its producer's stable name, never from mount order. */
12	export type EnvironmentId = Branded<'EnvironmentId'>
13	
14	/**
15	 * Merge-extensible map from environment kind to that kind's detail type. Each
16	 * producer package declares its kind by declaration merging; the registry
17	 * itself ships no kind.
18	 */
19	export interface EnvironmentKindMap {}
20	
21	/** Every declared environment kind; `string` while no producer has merged a kind into the program. */
22	export type EnvironmentKind = [keyof EnvironmentKindMap] extends [never] ? string : Extract<keyof EnvironmentKindMap, string>
23	
24	/** Kind-specific detail declared by the kind's producer; `unknown` for kinds outside this program. */
25	export type EnvironmentDetail<K extends string> = K extends keyof EnvironmentKindMap ? EnvironmentKindMap[K] : unknown
26	
27	/** Whether people curated an environment or an agent synthesized it. */
28	export type EnvironmentProvenance = 'curated' | 'synthesized'
29	
30	/** The work an environment asks of an agent. */
31	export interface EnvironmentTask {
32	  /** Complete task statement handed to the agent as its first user message. */
33	  readonly prompt: string
34	  /** Workspace fixture the runner mounts before the task starts, absent for a task that needs no files. */
35	  readonly fixture?: string
36	  /**
37	   * Workspace-relative paths the fixture supplies and the implementer must not
38	   * author — the tests, the reference outputs, and any overlaid check script.
39	   * Each is a `/`-separated relative path without `.` or `..` segments, naming
40	   * a file or a directory tree; the runner digests them beside the validator's
41	   * own directory and records a run that changed them as tampered.
42	   */
43	  readonly immutable?: readonly string[]
44	}
45	
46	/** One task with its verifiers, as the registry stores it. */
47	export interface EnvironmentDefinition<K extends EnvironmentKind = EnvironmentKind> {
48	  /** Stable identity across compositions. */
49	  readonly id: EnvironmentId
50	  /** Declared kind. */
51	  readonly kind: K
52	  /** Human-readable name. */
53	  readonly name: string
54	  /** What the task establishes, stated for people and models. */
55	  readonly description: string
56	  /** The task statement and its fixture. */
57	  readonly task: EnvironmentTask
58	  /**
59	   * Executable checks in the completion-standard vocabulary, each cased check
60	   * carrying the bodies its `cases` reference digests. A validator authors the
61	   * task's completion standard from exactly these checks, so evaluation and
62	   * production measure the same outcomes; authorship validates the bodies and
63	   * keeps only the reference in the log.
64	   */
65	  readonly checks: readonly AuthoredCheck[]
66	  /** Reserved for evaluation: never exported as training data and never shown to an implementer outside a run. */
67	  readonly heldOut: boolean
68	  /** Package that produced the registration. */
69	  readonly owner: string
70	  /** Curated by people or synthesized by an agent. */
71	  readonly provenance: EnvironmentProvenance
72	  /** Environment this one derived from, absent for roots. */
73	  readonly lineage?: EnvironmentId
74	  /** Kind-specific detail. */
75	  readonly detail: EnvironmentDetail<K>
76	}
77	
78	/** Selection over the registry's inventory; absent fields match everything. */
79	export interface EnvironmentFilter {
80	  /** Only environments of this kind. */
81	  readonly kind?: EnvironmentKind
82	  /** Only held-out (`true`) or only training-eligible (`false`) environments. */
83	  readonly heldOut?: boolean
84	}
85	
86	/** Model route one environment run used. */
87	export interface EnvironmentRunModel {
88	  /** Registered provider route. */
89	  readonly provider: string
90	  /** Provider-owned model id. */
91	  readonly model: string
92	}
93	
94	/** Content hashes of one environment as it was run; `fixtureSha256` is absent for a task without a fixture. */
95	export interface EnvironmentContentHashes {
96	  /** SHA-256 hex of the task prompt. */
97	  readonly promptSha256: string
98	  /**
99	   * SHA-256 hex of the check inventory in authored order: ids, outcomes, run
100	   * instructions, tree scopes, case references, and the case bodies themselves,
101	   * so changing one case changes the decontamination key.
102	   */
103	  readonly checksSha256: string
104	  /** SHA-256 hex over every fixture file (relative path and bytes, sorted). */
105	  readonly fixtureSha256?: string
106	  /** SHA-256 hex over the three hashes above; the decontamination key. */
107	  readonly contentSha256: string
108	}
109	
110	/**
111	 * Durable link from a session to the environment it ran, written by the
112	 * runner as the `environment/run` event before the run's first turn. Every
113	 * fold that groups, decontaminates, or ranks sessions by environment reads it
114	 * from the log instead of from an in-memory report.
115	 */
116	export interface EnvironmentRunStamp extends EnvironmentContentHashes {
117	  readonly kind: 'environment/run'
118	  readonly version: 1
119	  /** Environment that was run. */
120	  readonly environmentId: EnvironmentId
121	  /** Declared kind of the environment. */
122	  readonly environmentKind: string
123	  /** Whether the environment is reserved for evaluation; exports drop held-out sessions unless asked to keep them. */
124	  readonly heldOut: boolean
125	  /** Zero-based repetition of this environment inside its batch; paired designs match repetitions across variants. */
126	  readonly repetition: number
127	  /** Batch or sampling group the run belongs to, absent for a single run. */
128	  readonly group?: string
129	  /** District the run belongs to; exports withhold the districts a deployment configures by it, absent for a run outside every district. */
130	  readonly district?: string
131	  /** Model route the implementer ran on. */
132	  readonly model: EnvironmentRunModel
133	  /** Isolation the deployment declared for the run's checks. */
134	  readonly isolation: CertificateIsolation
135	}

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). - **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.

- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of the environment runner: the run request and the run report,
3	 * free of host-side imports.
4	 *
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types
6	 */
7	
8	import type { EnvironmentId, EnvironmentRunModel, EnvironmentRunStamp } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
9	import type { TokenUsage } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
10	import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
11	import type { CheckResult, VerificationCertificate } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
12	
13	/** One request to run a registered environment as one fresh session. */
14	export interface EnvironmentRunRequest {
15	  /** Registered environment to run. */
16	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
17	  /** Existing absolute directory the session is rooted at; the task fixture is overlaid onto it. */
18	  readonly workspace: string
19	  /** Model route for this run; absent uses the composition's default model selection. */
20	  readonly model?: EnvironmentRunModel
21	  /** Zero-based repetition of this environment inside its batch; absent means `0`. */
22	  readonly repetition?: number
23	  /** Batch or sampling group the run belongs to, absent for a single run. */
24	  readonly group?: string
25	  /** District the run belongs to, written into the stamp so exports can withhold it; absent for a run outside every district. */
26	  readonly district?: string
27	  /** Aborts the implementer's turns and the check commands when it fires. */
28	  readonly signal?: AbortSignal
29	}
30	
31	/**
32	 * One attempt: the implementer's turn followed by one run of the current
33	 * standard. The attempt's verdict is durable rather than reported: it is the
34	 * `verdict` of the `verification/run` this attempt recorded.
35	 */
36	export interface EnvironmentRunAttempt {
37	  /** One-based attempt number. */
38	  readonly attempt: number
39	  /** One result per active check, in the standard's check order; a tampered attempt executed none of them. */
40	  readonly results: readonly CheckResult[]
41	  /**
42	   * SHA-256 digest of the workspace as the validation began, after the fixture
43	   * was restored over it; a tampered attempt digests the workspace it refused
44	   * to measure, without restoring anything.
45	   */
46	  readonly treeHash: string
47	}
48	
49	/** Outcome of one environment run, returned after the session is flushed. */
50	export interface EnvironmentRunReport {
51	  /** Environment that was run. */
52	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
53	  /** Session the run created; its log is the durable record. */
54	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
55	  /** The `environment/run` stamp the session log carries, exactly as appended. */
56	  readonly stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp
57	  /** Every attempt in order; the last one decided `certified`. */
58	  readonly attempts: readonly EnvironmentRunAttempt[]
59	  /** Whether a run of the standard passed completely and the goal completed. */
60	  readonly certified: boolean
61	  /** Certificate of the passing run, present exactly when `certified` is `true`. */
62	  readonly certificate?: VerificationCertificate
63	  /** Model usage summed over every assistant message of the session, absent when the model produced none. */
64	  readonly usage?: TokenUsage
65	}

1	/**
2	 * Environment runner: the automated validator that runs one registered
3	 * environment as one fresh session. It stamps the session with the
4	 * environment it runs, authors the completion standard from the environment's
5	 * checks, drives the implementer turn by turn, restores the fixture and
6	 * executes the checks through the shell executor after each turn, records the
7	 * run, and completes the goal only under a certificate. The
8	 * [environment-runner Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-environment-runner.md)
9	 * owns the design rationale.
10	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner
11	 */
12	
13	import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto'
14	import { cp, mkdir, readdir, readFile, rm, stat, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
15	import { dirname, isAbsolute, join, relative, sep } from 'node:path'
16	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
17	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'

33	  CaseExitClass,

57	/** Stable error codes of a refused or broken run. */
58	export type EnvironmentRunErrorCode =
59	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT'
60	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_WORKSPACE'
61	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_FIXTURE'
62	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT'
63	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED'
64	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_STANDARD_LOST'
65	
66	/** Error returned by the environment runner boundary. */
67	export class EnvironmentRunError extends HarnessError {
68	  /**
69	   * @param message - human-readable reason.
70	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
71	   */
72	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
73	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
74	  constructor(message: string, code: EnvironmentRunErrorCode) {
75	    super(message, code)
76	  }
77	}
78	
79	/** Deployment choices of the runner, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
80	export interface Config {
81	  /** Isolation the deployment can defend for its check runs; written into every certificate and stamp. */
82	  isolation: CertificateIsolation
83	  /** Implementer turns before the run is reported uncertified; each is followed by one validation. */
84	  maxAttempts?: number
85	  /** Round cap handed to goal creation; absent applies the goal service default. */
86	  maxGoalRounds?: number
87	  /** Timeout override for each check command and each case, capped by the executor; absent applies the executor default. */
88	  checkTimeoutMs?: number
89	  /** Bound of each evidence string and of the directive detail. */
90	  evidenceMaxChars?: number
91	  /** Maximum failed cases one check result lists; the rest are counted and not named. */
92	  maxFailedCases?: number
93	}
94	
95	/** The runner's choices with every default applied. */
96	export interface ResolvedConfig {
97	  readonly isolation: CertificateIsolation
98	  readonly maxAttempts: number
99	  readonly maxGoalRounds: number | undefined
100	  readonly checkTimeoutMs: number | undefined
101	  readonly evidenceMaxChars: number
102	  readonly maxFailedCases: number
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * Apply the runner's defaults to a validated config.
107	 * @param config - validated deployment config.
108	 * @returns the resolved choices: one attempt, 2000 evidence characters, and 20 listed failed cases unless configured.
109	 */
110	export function resolveConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
111	  return {
112	    isolation: config.isolation,
113	    maxAttempts: config.maxAttempts ?? 1,
114	    maxGoalRounds: config.maxGoalRounds,
115	    checkTimeoutMs: config.checkTimeoutMs,
116	    evidenceMaxChars: config.evidenceMaxChars ?? 2000,
117	    maxFailedCases: config.maxFailedCases ?? 20,
118	  }
119	}
120	
121	/**
122	 * Characters a reserved check script's path may contain. The script is sourced
123	 * as the second word of the check command line, so the path must need no shell
124	 * quoting: quoting is dialect-specific and the runner does not know the composed
125	 * shell's dialect.
126	 */
127	const UNQUOTED_COMMAND_WORD = /^[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./\\-]+$/
128	
129	/** Key the check-owned digest records the reservation's tree under. */
130	const RESERVATION_KEY = '<reservation>'
131	
132	/** Subdirectory of a reservation holding one directory per check. */
133	const CHECKS_DIR = 'checks'
134	/** File inside a check's reserved directory holding its run instruction. */
135	const RUN_FILE = 'run'
136	/** File inside a check's reserved directory holding one case body per line. */
137	const CASES_FILE = 'cases.jsonl'
138	/** Reservation file holding the standard the current attempt measures. */
139	const STANDARD_FILE = 'standard.json'
140	/** Reservation subdirectory holding a held-out environment's fixture. */
141	const FIXTURE_DIR = 'fixture'
142	
143	/** A check id usable as one path segment of its reserved directory. */
144	const SAFE_CHECK_SEGMENT = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/
145	
146	/**
147	 * Absolute path of one check's reserved directory, which holds its run script
148	 * and its case bodies. A check id that is not a single path segment, and a
149	 * script path the check command line cannot carry unquoted, are both refused.
150	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation the barrier minted for this run.
151	 * @param checkId - the check's id, used verbatim as the directory's name.
152	 * @returns the absolute check directory.
153	 * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} when the id or the resulting path is unusable.
154	 */
155	function checkDirectory(runDirectory: string, checkId: string): string {
156	  if (!SAFE_CHECK_SEGMENT.test(checkId)) {
157	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`check "${checkId}" cannot name a reserved script file`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT')
158	  }
159	  const directory = join(runDirectory, CHECKS_DIR, checkId)
160	  if (!UNQUOTED_COMMAND_WORD.test(join(directory, RUN_FILE))) {
161	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`reserved check script "${join(directory, RUN_FILE)}" contains characters the check command line cannot carry unquoted`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT')
162	  }
163	  return directory
164	}
165	
166	/** Directory test that treats a missing or unreadable path as no directory. */
167	async function isDirectory(path: string): Promise<boolean> {
168	  try {
169	    return (await stat(path)).isDirectory()
170	  } catch {
171	    // stat rejects for a missing or unreadable path; both mean the caller named no usable directory.
172	    return false
173	  }
174	}
175	
176	/**
177	 * SHA-256 over every regular file under a directory: relative POSIX path, then
178	 * bytes, in sorted order. A case's `tree` channel passes its comparator's
179	 * normalizers, which are applied to each file's bytes before they are digested.
180	 */
181	async function hashDirectory(root: string, normalizers: readonly CheckCaseNormalizer[] = []): Promise<string> {
182	  const entries = await readdir(root, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })
183	  const files = entries.filter(entry => entry.isFile()).map(entry => join(entry.parentPath, entry.name)).sort()
184	  const hash = createHash('sha256')
185	  for (const file of files) {
186	    hash.update(relative(root, file).split(sep).join('/')).update('\0')
187	      .update(normalizeCaseBytes(await readFile(file), normalizers)).update('\0')
188	  }
189	  return hash.digest('hex')
190	}
191	
192	/** What one check-owned path digests to when nothing is there to read. */
193	const ABSENT_DIGEST = 'absent'
194	
195	/**
196	 * SHA-256 over one check-owned path: its tree when a directory, its bytes when
197	 * a file, and {@link ABSENT_DIGEST} when it is gone. Deleting a declared path
198	 * is as much a change to the check-owned set as rewriting it.
199	 * @param path - absolute path to digest.
200	 * @returns the digest, or the absent marker.
201	 */
202	async function hashCheckOwnedPath(path: string): Promise<string> {
203	  if (await isDirectory(path)) return hashDirectory(path)
204	  try {
205	    return createHash('sha256').update(await readFile(path)).digest('hex')
206	  } catch {
207	    // readFile rejects for a missing or unreadable path; either way the run
208	    // cannot read what the fixture supplied, which is the change to record.
209	    return ABSENT_DIGEST
210	  }
211	}
212	
213	/**
214	 * SHA-256 over the whole check-owned set: the validator's reserved directory,
215	 * when a barrier minted one, and every path the environment declared immutable,
216	 * each keyed by the name it is declared under.
217	 * @param workspace - the run's workspace directory, which immutable paths are relative to.
218	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation, absent when no barrier is composed.
219	 * @param immutable - the environment's declared immutable paths.
220	 * @returns one digest over the whole set.
221	 */
222	async function hashCheckOwned(
223	  workspace: string,
224	  runDirectory: string | undefined,
225	  immutable: readonly string[],
226	): Promise<string> {
227	  const hash = createHash('sha256')
228	  if (runDirectory !== undefined) {
229	    hash.update(RESERVATION_KEY).update('\0').update(await hashDirectory(runDirectory)).update('\0')
230	  }
231	  for (const path of immutable) {
232	    hash.update(path).update('\0').update(await hashCheckOwnedPath(join(workspace, path))).update('\0')
233	  }
234	  return hash.digest('hex')
235	}
236	
237	/**
238	 * Reject a workspace or fixture that is not an existing absolute directory,
239	 * then overlay the fixture and return its digest.
240	 * @returns the fixture digest, or `undefined` for a task without a fixture.
241	 */
242	async function prepareWorkspace(workspace: string, fixture: string | undefined): Promise<string | undefined> {
243	  if (!isAbsolute(workspace) || !await isDirectory(workspace)) {
244	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`workspace "${workspace}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_WORKSPACE')
245	  }
246	  if (fixture === undefined) return undefined
247	  if (!isAbsolute(fixture) || !await isDirectory(fixture)) {
248	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`fixture "${fixture}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_FIXTURE')
249	  }
250	  await cp(fixture, workspace, { recursive: true })
251	  return hashDirectory(fixture)
252	}
253	
254	/**
255	 * Overlay the fixture again so implementer edits to validator-owned files do
256	 * not reach the checks, then digest the workspace the validation will read.
257	 * @param workspace - the run's workspace directory.
258	 * @param fixture - the task fixture, absent for a task without one.
259	 * @returns the workspace digest as the validation begins.
260	 */
261	async function restoreFixture(workspace: string, fixture: string | undefined): Promise<string> {
262	  if (fixture !== undefined) await cp(fixture, workspace, { recursive: true })
263	  return hashDirectory(workspace)
264	}
265	
266	/**
267	 * Write the attempt's standard snapshot, one run script per active check, and
268	 * each cased check's bodies into the reservation, so what the checks execute
269	 * and what they measure live where the implementer cannot read them. The whole
270	 * reservation is inside the check-owned digest, which is what covers the case
271	 * bodies against tampering.
272	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation, absent when no barrier is composed.
273	 * @param standard - the standard this attempt measures.
274	 * @param bodies - case bodies per check id, from the environment definition.
275	 * @returns the script path per check id; empty without a reservation.
276	 * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} when a check id cannot name a script file.
277	 */
278	async function materializeChecks(
279	  runDirectory: string | undefined,
280	  standard: StandardView,
281	  bodies: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly CheckCase[]>,
282	): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
283	  const scripts = new Map<string, string>()
284	  if (runDirectory === undefined) return scripts
285	  await mkdir(join(runDirectory, CHECKS_DIR), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
286	  await writeFile(join(runDirectory, STANDARD_FILE), `${JSON.stringify(standard, null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 })
287	  for (const check of standard.checks) {
288	    const directory = checkDirectory(runDirectory, check.id)
289	    await mkdir(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
290	    const script = join(directory, RUN_FILE)
291	    await writeFile(script, `${check.run}\n`, { mode: 0o600 })
292	    const cases = bodies.get(check.id)
293	    if (cases !== undefined) {
294	      await writeFile(
295	        join(directory, CASES_FILE),

305	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
306	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
307	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted
308	}

310	/** Keep the first line and the tail of longer text inside the bound. */
311	function bound(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
312	  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text
313	  const newline = text.indexOf('\n')
314	  const head = newline === -1 ? text : text.slice(0, newline)
315	  const marker = '\n…'
316	  const tailBudget = maxChars - head.length - marker.length
317	  if (tailBudget <= 0) return text.slice(0, maxChars)
318	  return `${head}${marker}${text.slice(-tailBudget)}`
319	}

321	/** How one command ended, as the evidence states it. */
322	function exitLine(result: ShellRunResult): string {
323	  const exit = result.exitCode === null ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}` : `exit ${result.exitCode}`
324	  const cause = result.timedOut ? ` after the ${result.timeoutMs}ms timeout` : result.aborted ? ' after the run was aborted' : ''
325	  return `${exit}${cause}`
326	}

328	/** The captured output tails of one command, omitting an empty stream. */
329	function outputLines(result: ShellRunResult): string[] {
330	  const lines: string[] = []
331	  if (result.stdout.text !== '') lines.push(`stdout: ${result.stdout.text.trimEnd()}`)
332	  if (result.stderr.text !== '') lines.push(`stderr: ${result.stderr.text.trimEnd()}`)
333	  return lines
334	}
335	
336	/** Render one executed check's evidence: the exit fact, then the bounded output tails. */
337	function evidenceOf(result: ShellRunResult, maxChars: number): string {
338	  return bound([exitLine(result), ...outputLines(result)].join('\n'), maxChars)
339	}

341	/** How the candidate ended one case, as the directive clusters it. */
342	function exitClassOf(result: ShellRunResult): CaseExitClass {
343	  if (result.timedOut) return 'timeout'
344	  if (result.exitCode === null) return 'signal'
345	  return result.exitCode === 0 ? 'zero' : 'nonzero'
346	}

348	/** How each exit class reads in a cluster line. */
349	const EXIT_PHRASE: Readonly<Record<CaseExitClass, string>> = {
350	  zero: 'the program exited 0',
351	  nonzero: 'the program exited non-zero',
352	  signal: 'the program was terminated by a signal',
353	  timeout: 'the program exceeded the case timeout',

365	/** One check executed case by case: its tally and the failures behind it. */
366	interface CasedCheckRun {

374	/** Render one cased check's evidence: the tally, then each named failed case with its captured output. */
375	function casedEvidenceOf(run: CasedCheckRun, named: readonly CaseFailure[], maxChars: number): string {
376	  const lines = [`cases: ${run.passed} of ${run.total} passed (weight ${run.weightPassed} of ${run.weightTotal})`]
377	  for (const failure of named) {
378	    lines.push(`case "${failure.id}" differed on ${failure.channels.join(', ')}; ${exitLine(failure.result)}`)

384	/**
385	 * Whether one captured stream disagrees with its expected digest. A truncated
386	 * stream disagrees whatever it holds: the executor dropped bytes the digest
387	 * covers, so the comparison cannot be made.
388	 */
389	function streamMismatch(
390	  stream: ShellRunResult['stdout'],
391	  expected: string | undefined,
392	  normalizers: readonly CheckCaseNormalizer[],
393	): boolean {
394	  return stream.truncated || caseChannelDigest(Buffer.from(stream.text, 'utf8'), normalizers) !== expected

397	/**
398	 * The configured channels of one case whose observed value disagrees with the
399	 * case's expected digest, in the canonical channel order the log records.
400	 * @param body - the case that ran.
401	 * @param result - what the candidate produced.
402	 * @param scope - the absolute `treeScope` directory, absent for a check that declares none.
403	 * @returns the mismatching channels; empty when the case passed.
404	 */
405	async function caseMismatches(
406	  body: CheckCase,
407	  result: ShellRunResult,
408	  scope: string | undefined,
409	): Promise<CheckCaseChannel[]> {
410	  const { normalizers } = body.comparator
411	  const mismatched = new Set<CheckCaseChannel>()
412	  for (const channel of body.comparator.channels) {
413	    switch (channel) {
414	      case 'exit':
415	        if (result.exitCode !== body.expected.exitCode) mismatched.add(channel)
416	        break
417	      case 'stdout':
418	        if (streamMismatch(result.stdout, body.expected.stdoutSha256, normalizers)) mismatched.add(channel)
419	        break
420	      case 'stderr':
421	        if (streamMismatch(result.stderr, body.expected.stderrSha256, normalizers)) mismatched.add(channel)
422	        break
423	      case 'tree':
424	        // Authoring requires a treeScope for every check whose cases compare the tree.
425	        if (await hashDirectory(scope as string, normalizers) !== body.expected.treeSha256) mismatched.add(channel)
426	        break
427	      /* v8 ignore next 2 -- CheckCaseChannel is closed and every member is handled above */
428	      default:
429	        return assertNever(channel)
430	    }
431	  }
432	  return CHECK_CASE_CHANNELS.filter(channel => mismatched.has(channel))
433	}

435	/** One rendered cluster with the check facts its line names. */
436	interface RenderedCluster extends DirectiveCluster {
437	  readonly outcome: string
438	  readonly total: number
439	  readonly weightTotal: number
440	  readonly exitClass: CaseExitClass
441	}
442	
443	/** Group one cased check's failed cases by the channels that disagreed and how the candidate ended. */
444	function clustersOf(check: StandardCheck, result: CheckResult): RenderedCluster[] {
445	  const cases = result.cases
446	  /* v8 ignore next -- only a cased result reaches here, and a cased result carries its tally */
447	  if (cases === undefined) return []
448	  const clusters = new Map<string, RenderedCluster>()
449	  for (const failed of cases.failed) {
450	    const key = `${failed.exitClass}|${failed.channels.join(',')}`
451	    const existing = clusters.get(key)
452	    clusters.set(key, {
453	      checkId: result.checkId,
454	      channels: failed.channels,
455	      count: (existing?.count ?? 0) + 1,
456	      weight: (existing?.weight ?? 0) + failed.weight,
457	      outcome: check.outcome,
458	      total: cases.total,
459	      weightTotal: cases.weightTotal,
460	      exitClass: failed.exitClass,
461	    })
462	  }
463	  return [...clusters.values()]
464	}

466	/**
467	 * One directive per failed run. A cased check contributes one line per failure
468	 * cluster, naming its authored outcome, the cluster's count and weight, the
469	 * channels that disagreed, and how the candidate ended — never a case body, an
470	 * expected digest, or a byte of captured output. A check without cases
471	 * contributes its recorded evidence line.
472	 * @param failures - the run's failing results, in check order.
473	 * @param checks - the standard's active checks, supplying each outcome text.
474	 * @param maxChars - bound of the rendered detail.
475	 * @returns the directive, carrying `clusters` when a cased check failed.
476	 */
477	function describeFailures(
478	  failures: readonly CheckResult[],
479	  checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
480	  maxChars: number,
481	): DirectiveRequest {
482	  const lines: string[] = []
483	  const clusters: DirectiveCluster[] = []
484	  for (const failure of failures) {
485	    const check = checks.find(candidate => candidate.id === failure.checkId)
486	    if (check === undefined || failure.cases === undefined) {
487	      lines.push(failure.evidence)
488	      continue
489	    }
490	    for (const cluster of clustersOf(check, failure)) {
491	      clusters.push({ checkId: cluster.checkId, channels: cluster.channels, count: cluster.count, weight: cluster.weight })
492	      lines.push(`${cluster.outcome}: ${cluster.count} of ${cluster.total} cases failed (weight ${cluster.weight} of ${cluster.weightTotal}); mismatching channels: ${cluster.channels.join(', ')}; ${EXIT_PHRASE[cluster.exitClass]}`)
493	    }
494	  }
495	  return {
496	    rootCause: `${failures.length} of the standard's checks failed`,
497	    detail: bound(lines.map((line, index) => `${index + 1}. ${line}`).join('\n'), maxChars),
498	    ...clusters.length === 0 ? {} : { clusters },
499	  }
500	}

502	/**
503	 * The one directive a tampered attempt issues. A digest comparison knows that
504	 * the check-owned set changed and nothing else, so the text names neither a
505	 * path nor a check: it states that the measurement is void and that the run is
506	 * over. Pinned verbatim by the runner README and the `read-barrier-tamper`
507	 * snapshot.
508	 */
509	const TAMPER_DIRECTIVE: DirectiveRequest = {
510	  rootCause: 'the files this task is measured with were modified during the attempt',
511	  detail: 'Those files belong to the validator: the task is to make them pass, never to change them. This run is void and no certificate can follow it.',
512	}
513	
514	/** The evidence every check of a tampered attempt records, since none of them ran. */
515	const TAMPER_EVIDENCE = 'not executed: the files this task is measured with were modified during the attempt'
516	
517	/** The validator's follow-up turn after a failed run; the text is pinned by the runner README and its e2e. */
518	function followupText(directive: DirectiveRequest): string {
519	  return `<validation_failed>\n${directive.rootCause}\n${directive.detail}\nContinue working on the task; the validator runs again when you stop.\n</validation_failed>`
520	}

522	/** Sum the usage of every assistant message in a session log. */
523	function totalUsage(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TokenUsage | undefined {
524	  const steps = events.flatMap(event => (
525	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined ? [event.data.usage] : []
526	  ))
527	  if (steps.length === 0) return undefined
528	  const total: TokenUsage = {
529	    inputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.inputTokens, 0),
530	    outputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.outputTokens, 0),
531	  }
532	  for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens'] as const) {
533	    const values = steps.flatMap((step) => {
534	      const value = step[key]
535	      return value === undefined ? [] : [value]
536	    })
537	    if (values.length > 0) total[key] = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)
538	  }
539	  return total
540	}

611	  /** Stamp, goal, standard, then the attempt loop; the session is flushed on every path. */
612	  private async drive(
613	    agent: Agent,
614	    definition: EnvironmentDefinition,
615	    stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp,
616	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
617	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
618	    const { goals, completionStandards, sessions } = this.ctx
619	    await agent.whenIdle()
620	    const runDirectory = await this.reserve(agent, definition)
621	    agent.session.append('environment/run', stamp)
622	    const goal = goals.create(agent, {
623	      objective: definition.task.prompt,
624	      ...this.resolved.maxGoalRounds === undefined ? {} : { maxGoalRounds: this.resolved.maxGoalRounds },
625	    })
626	    goals.disarm(agent)
627	    const authored = completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: definition.checks })
628	    // Authorship validated every case against the reference it carries and kept
629	    // the reference alone; the bodies stay here, for the reservation and the
630	    // per-case execution.
631	    const bodies = new Map(definition.checks.flatMap(check => (
632	      check.caseBodies === undefined ? [] : [[check.id, check.caseBodies] as const]
633	    )))
634	    const immutable = definition.task.immutable ?? []
635	    // Stock the reservation and digest the check-owned set before the
636	    // implementer's first turn: that digest is what every later attempt is
637	    // compared against.
638	    await materializeChecks(runDirectory, authored, bodies)
639	    let checkOwned = await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable)
640	    const attempts: EnvironmentRunAttempt[] = []
641	    let certificate: VerificationCertificate | undefined
642	    let prompt = definition.task.prompt
643	    try {
644	      for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= this.resolved.maxAttempts; attempt += 1) {
645	        await this.deliver(agent, prompt)
646	        const standard = this.currentStandard(agent, goal.id)
647	        const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }
648	        if (await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable) !== checkOwned) {
649	          attempts.push(await this.recordTamper(agent, standard, ref, request.workspace, attempt))
650	          break
651	        }
652	        const treeHash = await restoreFixture(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
653	        const scripts = await materializeChecks(runDirectory, standard, bodies)
654	        // The validator just rewrote its own directory, so the set it now owns
655	        // is the baseline the next attempt must still find.
656	        checkOwned = await hashCheckOwned(request.workspace, runDirectory, immutable)
657	        const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, request, scripts, bodies)
658	        const outcome = completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, this.resolved.isolation, results, {
659	          executor: 'runner',
660	          treeHash,
661	        })
662	        attempts.push({ attempt, results, treeHash })
663	        if (outcome.certified) {
664	          certificate = outcome.certificate
665	          const current = goals.get(agent)
666	          if (current === undefined || current.id !== goal.id) {
667	            throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the implementer replaced goal "${goal.id}"`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED')
668	          }
669	          goals.complete(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })
670	          break
671	        }
672	        const directive = describeFailures(outcome.failures, standard.checks, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars)
673	        completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, directive)
674	        prompt = followupText(directive)
675	      }
676	    } finally {
677	      await sessions.flush(agent.session)
678	    }
679	    const usage = totalUsage(agent.session.events)
680	    return {
681	      environment: definition.id,
682	      sessionId: agent.id,
683	      stamp,
684	      attempts,
685	      certified: certificate !== undefined,
686	      ...certificate === undefined ? {} : { certificate },
687	      ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage },
688	    }
689	  }

839	    for (const body of cases) {
840	      const scope = check.treeScope === undefined ? undefined : join(request.workspace, check.treeScope)
841	      if (scope !== undefined) {
842	        await rm(scope, { recursive: true, force: true })
843	        await mkdir(scope, { recursive: true })
844	      }
845	      for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(body.input.files ?? {})) {
846	        const staged = join(request.workspace, path)
847	        await mkdir(dirname(staged), { recursive: true })
848	        await writeFile(staged, content)
849	      }
850	      const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(
851	        this.caseSpec([command, ...body.input.argv].join(' '), request, body.input.stdin),
852	      )
853	      const channels = await caseMismatches(body, result, scope)
854	      if (channels.length === 0) {
855	        passedCases += 1
856	        weightPassed += body.weight
857	        continue
858	      }
859	      failures.push({ id: body.id, weight: body.weight, channels, exitClass: exitClassOf(result), result })
860	    }
861	    return {
862	      passed: passedCases,
863	      total: cases.length,
864	      weightPassed,
865	      weightTotal: cases.reduce((sum, body) => sum + body.weight, 0),
866	      failures,
867	    }
868	  }
869	}
