1	/**
2	 * Conversation call configuration and freeze utilities. Provider routing,
3	 * model, reasoning effort, and sampling values are request-header state that
4	 * can affect cache reuse; request waterfalls replace them and the loop logs
5	 * changed snapshots instead of allowing silent per-call drift.
6	 * @module dsh-llm/call-config
7	 */
8	
9	import type { GenerateOptions } from './types.ts'
10	import type { ReasoningEffortId } from './brand.ts'
11	
12	/** Process-local identities of request objects assembled by dsh-agent-loop. */
13	const AGENT_LOOP_REQUESTS = new WeakSet<GenerateOptions>()
14	
15	// TODO(call-config-shape): Revisit which fields are epoch-level for cache reuse
16	// and where provider-specific request options belong.
17	/**
18	 * Provider, model, reasoning effort, and sampling scalars of one conversation's
19	 * requests. Every field maps 1:1 onto the same-named `GenerateOptions` field;
20	 * the loop builds requests from the logged header rather than accepting these
21	 * per call.
22	 */
23	export interface LlmCallConfig {
24	  provider: string
25	  model: string
26	  reasoningEffort?: ReasoningEffortId
27	  temperature?: number
28	  maxTokens?: number
29	  stop?: string[]
30	}
31	
32	/**
33	 * Effective config fields supplied by exact-model adapter resolution rather
34	 * than by the caller's request proposal.
35	 */
36	export interface LlmCallConfigAdapterDefaults {
37	  reasoningEffort?: true
38	  maxTokens?: true
39	}
40	
41	/**
42	 * Field-wise equality over {@link LlmCallConfig} — the comparison a caller
43	 * runs to decide whether a proposed configuration is a real change (worth a
44	 * logged header snapshot) or the held one restated.
45	 * @param a - one configuration.
46	 * @param b - the other.
47	 * @returns whether every field (including the `stop` list, element-wise) matches.
48	 */
49	export function callConfigEquals(a: LlmCallConfig, b: LlmCallConfig): boolean {
50	  if (
51	    a.provider !== b.provider
52	    || a.model !== b.model
53	    || a.reasoningEffort !== b.reasoningEffort
54	    || a.temperature !== b.temperature
55	    || a.maxTokens !== b.maxTokens
56	  ) return false
57	  if (a.stop === undefined || b.stop === undefined) return a.stop === b.stop
58	  return a.stop.length === b.stop.length && a.stop.every((s, i) => s === b.stop?.[i])
59	}
60	
61	/**
62	 * Mark one exact request object as assembled by dsh-agent-loop.
63	 * @param request - loop-owned request envelope before LLM dispatch.
64	 * @returns the same request object marked as created by the process-local agent loop.
65	 */
66	export function markAgentLoopRequest<T extends GenerateOptions>(request: T): T {
67	  AGENT_LOOP_REQUESTS.add(request)
68	  return request
69	}
70	
71	/**
72	 * Test whether the exact request object was assembled by dsh-agent-loop.
73	 * @param request - request envelope observed at the LLM waterfall.
74	 * @returns whether {@link markAgentLoopRequest} recorded this object.
75	 */
76	export function isAgentLoopRequest(request: GenerateOptions): boolean {
77	  return AGENT_LOOP_REQUESTS.has(request)
78	}
79	
80	/**
81	 * Deep-freeze a value in place with an iterative traversal, guarding cycles,
82	 * so later mutation throws without imposing a JavaScript call-stack depth cap.
83	 * {@link AbortSignal} objects are deliberately skipped because they are the
84	 * request's live cancellation channel and freezing them breaks abort.
85	 * @param value - the value to freeze in place.
86	 * @returns the same value, frozen.
87	 */
88	export function deepFreeze<T>(value: T): T {
89	  const seen = new WeakSet<object>()
90	  const pending: (
91	    | { kind: 'visit'; node: unknown }
92	    | { kind: 'property'; source: Record<string, unknown>; key: string }
93	  )[] = [{ kind: 'visit', node: value }]
94	  while (pending.length > 0) {
95	    const task = pending.pop()
96	    /* v8 ignore next -- the loop condition guarantees one pending task. */
97	    if (task === undefined) continue
98	    if (task.kind === 'property') {
99	      pending.push({ kind: 'visit', node: task.source[task.key] })
100	      continue
101	    }
102	    const node = task.node
103	    if (node === null || typeof node !== 'object') continue
104	    if (node instanceof AbortSignal) continue
105	    if (seen.has(node)) continue
106	    seen.add(node)
107	    Object.freeze(node)
108	    const keys = Object.keys(node)
109	    for (let index = keys.length - 1; index >= 0; index--) {
110	      const key = keys[index]
111	      /* v8 ignore next -- the loop is bounded by the captured key count. */
112	      if (key === undefined) continue
113	      pending.push({ kind: 'property', source: node as Record<string, unknown>, key })
114	    }
115	  }
116	  return value
117	}

1	/**
2	 * Request-header reconstruction utilities over full `request/header` session
3	 * events. Anyone holding a session log reconstructs the {@link EpochHeader}
4	 * any request was built under by taking the latest canonical snapshot; the
5	 * loop uses the same equality helper to avoid logging unchanged headers.
6	 *
7	 * @module dsh-session/request-header
8	 */
9	
10	import { callConfigEquals } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
11	import type { ToolSchema } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { EpochHeader, SessionEvent } from './types.ts'
13	
14	/**
15	 * Normalize a header to canonical form: an empty system prompt and empty tool
16	 * list become absent fields, matching how requests are built. Logging, folding,
17	 * and comparison use this one representation.
18	 * @param header - the header to normalize (not mutated).
19	 * @returns the canonical header.
20	 */
21	export function canonicalHeader(header: EpochHeader): EpochHeader {
22	  const adapterDefaults = header.adapterDefaults
23	  return {
24	    config: header.config,
25	    ...adapterDefaults?.reasoningEffort === true || adapterDefaults?.maxTokens === true
26	      ? { adapterDefaults }
27	      : {},
28	    ...header.system !== undefined && header.system.length > 0 ? { system: header.system } : {},
29	    ...header.tools !== undefined && header.tools.length > 0 ? { tools: header.tools } : {},
30	  }
31	}
32	
33	/** Canonical JSON equality for tool schemas assembled through the same path. */
34	function sameSchema(a: ToolSchema, b: ToolSchema): boolean {
35	  return JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b)
36	}
37	
38	/**
39	 * Field-wise equality over canonical headers. Tool schemas compare in order.
40	 * @param a - one canonical header.
41	 * @param b - the other.
42	 * @returns whether config, system, and tools all match.
43	 */
44	export function headerEquals(a: EpochHeader, b: EpochHeader): boolean {
45	  if (
46	    !callConfigEquals(a.config, b.config)
47	    || a.adapterDefaults?.reasoningEffort !== b.adapterDefaults?.reasoningEffort
48	    || a.adapterDefaults?.maxTokens !== b.adapterDefaults?.maxTokens
49	    || a.system !== b.system
50	  ) return false
51	  const at = a.tools ?? []
52	  const bt = b.tools ?? []
53	  return at.length === bt.length && at.every((tool, i) => sameSchema(tool, bt[i] as ToolSchema))
54	}
55	
56	/**
57	 * Fold the header events of a log (or any prefix) into the
58	 * {@link EpochHeader} in force after the last snapshot. Non-header events are
59	 * skipped. This is the pure offline reconstruction path; the live session
60	 * tracks the same fold incrementally.
61	 * @param events - session events in log order.
62	 * @param from - a previously folded state to continue from.
63	 * @returns the latest canonical header, or undefined when none exists yet.
64	 */
65	export function foldRequestHeader(events: readonly SessionEvent[], from?: EpochHeader): EpochHeader | undefined {
66	  let state = from
67	  for (const event of events) {
68	    if (event.type === 'request/header') state = canonicalHeader(event.data.header)
69	  }
70	  return state
71	}

3	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent/model-selection
4	 */
5	
6	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
7	import type { LlmCallConfig, ReasoningEffortId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
8	
9	/** Complete provider, model, and optional reasoning effort selected for one live Agent. */
10	export interface ModelSelection {
11	  /** Registered provider route. */
12	  provider: string
13	  /** Provider-owned model id. */
14	  model: string
15	  /** Adapter-owned reasoning effort, or provider/default behavior when absent. */
16	  reasoningEffort?: ReasoningEffortId
17	}
18	
19	/** Mutable model selection plus the value captured for the current step. */
20	export interface ModelSelectionRef {
21	  /** Model selected for the next step that enters prompt assembly. */
22	  current: ModelSelection | undefined
23	  /** Selection captured when the current step entered prompt assembly. */
24	  assembled: ModelSelection | undefined
25	}
26	
27	/**
28	 * Couple one mutable selection to Agent-scoped prompt assembly and request routing.
29	 * Prompt assembly snapshots the selected model before delegating, then applies
30	 * its provider/model pair and effort to request config so a
31	 * concurrent switch takes effect on a later step instead of splitting the two
32	 * surfaces. An absent selected effort clears any inherited effort, restoring
33	 * the selected model's provider/default behavior.
34	 *
35	 * @param agentCtx - The selected Agent's scoped context.
36	 * @param selection - Mutable selection owned by the calling entry point.
37	 * @returns Disposer for both scoped waterfall listeners.
38	 */
39	export function installModelSelection(agentCtx: Context, selection: ModelSelectionRef): () => void {
40	  const disposeAssembly = agentCtx.on('system-prompt/assemble', async (_assembly, _context, next) => {
41	    const selected = selection.current
42	    const assembled = await next()
43	    selection.assembled = selected
44	    if (selected === undefined) return assembled
45	    return {
46	      ...assembled,
47	      variables: {
48	        ...assembled.variables,
49	        provider: selected.provider,
50	        model: selected.model,
51	      },
52	    }
53	  })
54	  const disposeRequest = agentCtx.on(
55	    'agent/request',
56	    async (_payload, next): Promise<LlmCallConfig> => {
57	      const resolved = await next()
58	      const selected = selection.assembled
59	      if (selected === undefined) return resolved
60	      const { reasoningEffort: _inheritedEffort, ...withoutInheritedEffort } = resolved
61	      return {
62	        ...withoutInheritedEffort,
63	        provider: selected.provider,
64	        model: selected.model,
65	        ...selected.reasoningEffort === undefined
66	          ? {}
67	          : { reasoningEffort: selected.reasoningEffort },
68	      }
69	    },
70	  )
71	  return () => {
72	    disposeAssembly()
73	    disposeRequest()
74	  }
75	}

Integration (stage 8) is itself a goal whose standard runs against the merged head, so a certificate never goes stale at merge; release (stage 10) signs the certificate on that merged head together with the review and the changelog, and deployment happens under that signature, never on an agent's initiative.

The project's own checks become `synthesized` environments only after admission — failing on the pre-state, passing on the reference, a gaming agent failing to certify — and a human assigns the training split before anything trains on them.

### W3 — Environment-first model pipeline

Goal 3 — a roughly 120B-parameter open-weight model trained with RLVR that beats frontier models on the fleet's tasks. The unit of data is a group of rollouts of one environment under one policy version, produced on demand by the runner. Fleet sessions feed a short SFT cold start and the environment factory; RL rewards come from hidden checks on a pristine fixture plus the patch, and every artefact down to the model card is generated from the same records.

| Stage | Actor | Type | Status | Emits | Plugins | On failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Environment factory | Environment Synthesizer + Data Curator | DS | proposed | `EnvironmentProposal`, `EnvironmentAdmission` | existing: environments; new: curator (admission, hashes), `hiddenChecks` on `EnvironmentDefinition` | A task whose reference does not pass, or whose pre-state does not fail, is not admitted. |
| 2. Calibration | Evaluator | D | partial | `EnvironmentStats` | existing: environment-runner, scorekeeper (the `EnvironmentStats` fold); new: policy-version keying, N repetitions natively in the runner | An environment with no group run has no measured difficulty and is not sampled. |
| 3. Export and curation | Data Curator | D | proposed | `ExportManifest`, `DatasetManifest` | existing: trajectories, session-telemetry redaction; new: curator plugin, shipped redaction rules, consent and licence events | A sample whose consent scope is unknown is dropped, never assumed. |
| 4. SFT cold start | Trainer Operator | D | proposed | `SplitManifest`, `TrainingRun` | existing: jobs, schedule; new: trainer-operator plugin, `role` field on trajectories | A run whose data hashes do not match the manifest is refused. |
| 5. Reinforcement learning | Trainer Operator | D (outside the session log) | proposed | `TrainingRun` | existing: subprocess; new: trainer-operator plugin, correlation headers on the LLM seam, pristine-fixture reward in the runner, `rl-minimal` preset | A run whose reward source is not a `verification/run` event is refused. |
| 6. Held-out evaluation | Evaluator | D | proposed | `EvalReport` | existing: environment-runner, agent-default-model; new: harness-variant pinning in `EvalReport` | An evaluation on an unpinned harness variant is not comparable and is rejected. |
| 7. Safety and alignment | Evaluator + disinterested judges | DS | proposed | `SafetyReport` | new: oversight seam, safety suites as environments | A hold verdict stops promotion. |
| 8. Model lineage and release | Attributed human signer (accountable officer) | HUMAN | proposed | `ModelLineage`, `ModelRelease`, `SignoffRecord` | existing: approval seam; new: model registry plugin, `ModelLineage` record | A rejection records which suite failed. |
| 9. Recalibration and feedback | Scorekeeper | STORE | partial | `EnvironmentStats`, `ScoreboardBatch` | existing: trajectories, scorekeeper; new: policy-version keying | — feeds W3's own calibration and W4 facts. |

The unit of data is a group of rollouts of one environment under one policy version, produced by the runner on demand, not a fleet session harvested after the fact; fleet sessions instead feed a short SFT cold start (including validator and diagnostician role sessions with deterministic rewards) and the environment factory.

Reinforcement learning (stage 5) runs outside the session log: the reward is computed on a pristine fixture plus the implementer's patch under host isolation with hidden checks, so any write under check-owned paths is a tamper verdict with reward zero, and truncated, aborted, or errored rollouts are masked rather than scored as failures; a correlation header on the LLM seam lets the trainer's inference proxy join token ids and logprobs to the session, turn, and step that produced them.

Held-out evaluation (stage 6) pins the harness variant so a checkpoint is never measured against a harness that co-evolved with it, and safety and alignment (stage 7) freezes every mitigation plan before it runs so nothing grades itself; the accountable officer's `ModelLineage` record generates the Article 53 documentation and fires an alarm at a configured fraction of the systemic-risk compute threshold.

### W4 — Fleet observatory and two-speed improvement

Goal 4 — the loop that feeds both the harness and the model. A fast loop where agents write and refine skills in their department layer under a deterministic keep-or-retire scoreboard, and a slow loop where frozen experiments and attributable humans move knowledge into the fleet. Both read one content-addressed ledger; the observatory is a projection of the log, not a pipeline beside it.

125	/** Run `tasks` with at most `limit` in flight, keeping results in task order. */
126	async function bounded<T>(tasks: readonly (() => Promise<T>)[], limit: number): Promise<T[]> {
127	  const results = new Array<T>(tasks.length)
128	  let next = 0
129	  const worker = async (): Promise<void> => {
130	    while (next < tasks.length) {
131	      const index = next
132	      next += 1
133	      results[index] = await (tasks[index] as () => Promise<T>)()
134	    }
135	  }
136	  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(limit, tasks.length) }, worker))
137	  return results
138	}

145	/**
146	 * Running state of one plan: the consecutive errors each model route has
147	 * produced and the spend the reported cells have folded. Both are read as a
148	 * cell is about to start, so a refusal only ever keeps an unstarted cell out of
149	 * the runner and never interrupts one in flight.
150	 */
151	class PlanLedger {
152	  private readonly consecutiveErrors = new Map<string, number>()
153	  private inputTokens = 0
154	  private outputTokens = 0
155	
156	  constructor(
157	    private readonly breaker: RouteBreakerConfig | undefined,
158	    private readonly ceiling: number | undefined,
159	  ) {}
160	
161	  /** Model usage of every cell folded so far. */
162	  get spend(): FleetSpend {
163	    return { inputTokens: this.inputTokens, outputTokens: this.outputTokens }
164	  }
165	
166	  /**
167	   * The refusal that keeps a cell out of the runner.
168	   * @param cell - the cell about to start.
169	   * @returns the error to record for the cell, or `undefined` when nothing refuses it.
170	   */
171	  refusal(cell: FleetCell): FleetCellError | undefined {
172	    const spent = this.inputTokens + this.outputTokens
173	    if (this.ceiling !== undefined && spent >= this.ceiling) {
174	      return {
175	        code: 'FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED' satisfies FleetCellErrorCode,
176	        message: `the plan's token ceiling of ${this.ceiling} was reached at ${spent} tokens`,
177	      }
178	    }
179	    const errors = this.consecutiveErrors.get(routeName(cell.model)) ?? 0
180	    if (this.breaker !== undefined && errors >= this.breaker.consecutiveErrors) {
181	      return {
182	        code: 'FLEET_ROUTE_BREAKER_OPEN' satisfies FleetCellErrorCode,
183	        message: `route ${routeName(cell.model)} stopped after ${errors} consecutive errors`,
184	      }
185	    }
186	    return undefined
187	  }
188	
189	  /**
190	   * Fold one outcome the runner produced. A refused cell never reaches this,
191	   * so a refusal neither opens another route's breaker nor moves the spend.
192	   * @param outcome - the settled outcome of one cell the runner handled.
193	   */
194	  record(outcome: FleetCellOutcome): void {
195	    const route = routeName(outcome.cell.model)
196	    if ('error' in outcome) {
197	      this.consecutiveErrors.set(route, (this.consecutiveErrors.get(route) ?? 0) + 1)
198	      return
199	    }
200	    this.consecutiveErrors.set(route, 0)
201	    this.inputTokens += outcome.report.usage?.inputTokens ?? 0
202	    this.outputTokens += outcome.report.usage?.outputTokens ?? 0
203	  }
204	}

216	function restrict(enumerated: readonly FleetCell[], selected: readonly FleetCell[]): FleetCell[] {
217	  if (selected.length === 0) throw new FleetError('the plan names no cell to run', 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
218	  const wanted = new Set(selected.map(fleetCellKey))
219	  const kept = enumerated.filter(cell => wanted.has(fleetCellKey(cell)))
220	  for (const key of kept.map(fleetCellKey)) wanted.delete(key)
221	  const unenumerated = [...wanted]
222	  if (unenumerated.length > 0) {
223	    throw new FleetError(`cell "${unenumerated[0] as string}" is not one this plan enumerates`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
224	  }
225	  return kept
226	}

240	/** Fold the leaderboard from the cell outcomes, one row per model route and environment. */
241	function foldLeaderboard(
242	  outcomes: readonly FleetCellOutcome[],
243	  definitions: ReadonlyMap<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentDefinition>,
244	): LeaderboardRow[] {
245	  const rows = new Map<string, LeaderboardRow>()
246	  for (const outcome of outcomes) {
247	    const key = rowKey(outcome.cell)
248	    const definition = definitions.get(outcome.cell.environment) as EnvironmentDefinition
249	    const row = rows.get(key) ?? {
250	      provider: outcome.cell.model.provider,
251	      model: outcome.cell.model.model,
252	      environmentId: outcome.cell.environment,
253	      environmentKind: definition.kind,
254	      heldOut: definition.heldOut,
255	      runs: 0,
256	      errors: 0,
257	      certified: 0,
258	      certificateRate: 0,
259	      attemptsMean: 0,
260	      inputTokens: 0,
261	      outputTokens: 0,
262	    }
263	    rows.set(key, 'report' in outcome ? withReport(row, outcome.report) : { ...row, errors: row.errors + 1 })
264	  }
265	  return [...rows.values()]
266	}

268	/** Add one report to a row, recomputing the derived rates. */
269	function withReport(row: LeaderboardRow, report: EnvironmentRunReport): LeaderboardRow {
270	  const runs = row.runs + 1
271	  const certified = row.certified + (report.certified ? 1 : 0)
272	  const attempts = row.attemptsMean * row.runs + report.attempts.length
273	  return {
274	    ...row,
275	    isolation: report.stamp.isolation,
276	    runs,
277	    certified,
278	    certificateRate: certified / runs,
279	    attemptsMean: attempts / runs,
280	    inputTokens: row.inputTokens + (report.usage?.inputTokens ?? 0),
281	    outputTokens: row.outputTokens + (report.usage?.outputTokens ?? 0),
282	  }
283	}

285	/**

290	export function leaderboardMarkdown(report: FleetRunReport): string {

292	  const rule = '|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|'
293	  const lines = report.leaderboard.map(row => (
294	    `| ${row.provider}/${row.model} | ${row.environmentId} | ${row.heldOut ? 'yes' : 'no'} | ${row.isolation ?? '-'} | ${row.runs} | ${row.errors} | ${row.certified} | ${row.certificateRate.toFixed(2)} | ${row.attemptsMean.toFixed(2)} | ${row.inputTokens} / ${row.outputTokens} |`
295	  ))
296	  return [`Fleet run \`${report.group}\``, '', header, rule, ...lines].join('\n') + '\n'
297	}

299	/** Fleet runs (`ctx.fleet`): a plan of environment cells through the runner, with a leaderboard. */
300	export class FleetService extends Service {
301	  static inject = ['environments', 'environmentRuns', 'agentDefaultModel']
302	
303	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
304	    maxConcurrent: z.natural().min(1).default(1),
305	    // Prevent Schemastery from materializing an omitted routeBreaker as `{}`,
306	    // whose missing `consecutiveErrors` would reject every breakerless deployment.
307	    routeBreaker: z.object({
308	      consecutiveErrors: z.natural().min(1).required(),
309	    }).default(undefined as unknown as RouteBreakerConfig),
310	    workspaceRetention: z.union(['keep', 'remove-certified', 'remove-all'] as const).required(),
311	  })
312	
313	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
314	
315	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
316	    super(ctx, 'fleet')
317	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
318	  }
319	
320	  /**
321	   * Run every cell of a plan and fold the leaderboard. A cell whose run
322	   * throws is kept as an error outcome, as is a cell the route breaker or the
323	   * token ceiling refused to start; the fleet run itself rejects only for a
324	   * plan it cannot start.
325	   * @param plan - environments, model routes, repetitions, an optional exact
326	   *   cell selection, workspace root, group, district, token ceiling, and abort signal.
327	   * @returns every cell's outcome in plan order, the leaderboard folded from the reports, and the run's spend.
328	   * @throws {@link FleetError} when the plan selects no environment, asks for
329	   *   no repetition, names no or an unenumerated cell, or sets a token ceiling
330	   *   that is not a positive integer.
331	   */
332	  async run(plan: FleetPlan): Promise<FleetRunReport> {
333	    if (!Number.isInteger(plan.repetitions) || plan.repetitions < 1) {
334	      throw new FleetError(`repetitions must be a positive integer, got ${String(plan.repetitions)}`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
335	    }
336	    if (plan.tokenCeiling !== undefined && (!Number.isInteger(plan.tokenCeiling) || plan.tokenCeiling < 1)) {
337	      throw new FleetError(`tokenCeiling must be a positive integer, got ${String(plan.tokenCeiling)}`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
338	    }
339	    const definitions = this.select(plan)
340	    if (definitions.size === 0) throw new FleetError('the plan selects no environment', 'FLEET_EMPTY_PLAN')
341	    const models = plan.models.length === 0 ? [this.defaultModel()] : plan.models
342	    const group = plan.group ?? `fleet-${randomUUID()}`
343	    const enumerated: FleetCell[] = []
344	    for (const environment of definitions.keys()) {
345	      for (const model of models) {
346	        for (let repetition = 0; repetition < plan.repetitions; repetition += 1) enumerated.push({ environment, model, repetition })
347	      }
348	    }
349	    const cells = plan.cells === undefined ? enumerated : restrict(enumerated, plan.cells)
350	    const ledger = new PlanLedger(this.resolved.routeBreaker, plan.tokenCeiling)
351	    const tasks = cells.map(cell => () => this.runCell(cell, plan, group, ledger))
352	    const outcomes = await bounded(tasks, this.resolved.maxConcurrent)
353	    return { group, cells: outcomes, leaderboard: foldLeaderboard(outcomes, definitions), spend: ledger.spend }
354	  }
355	
356	  /** Resolve the plan's environment selection against the registry, in registry order. */
357	  private select(plan: FleetPlan): Map<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentDefinition> {
358	    const selected = 'ids' in plan.environments
359	      ? plan.environments.ids.flatMap((id) => {
360	        const definition = this.ctx.environments.get(id)
361	        if (definition === undefined) throw new FleetError(`environment "${id}" is not registered`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
362	        return [definition]
363	      })
364	      : this.ctx.environments.list(plan.environments.filter)
365	    return new Map(selected.map(definition => [definition.id, definition]))
366	  }
367	
368	  /** The composition's default model route, detached from the selection service. */
369	  private defaultModel(): EnvironmentRunModel {
370	    const selection = this.ctx.agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()
371	    return { provider: selection.provider, model: selection.model }
372	  }
373	
374	  /**
375	   * Run one cell unless the ledger refuses it, fold the outcome back into the
376	   * ledger, and apply the configured workspace retention.
377	   */
378	  private async runCell(cell: FleetCell, plan: FleetPlan, group: string, ledger: PlanLedger): Promise<FleetCellOutcome> {
379	    const refusal = ledger.refusal(cell)
380	    if (refusal !== undefined) return this.settle({ cell, error: refusal }, plan, group)
381	    const { outcome, workspace } = await this.execute(cell, plan, group)
382	    ledger.record(outcome)
383	    if (workspace !== undefined && this.removes(outcome)) await rm(workspace, { recursive: true, force: true })
384	    return this.settle(outcome, plan, group)
385	  }
386	
387	  /** Announce one settled cell after its workspace retention has run. */
388	  private settle(outcome: FleetCellOutcome, plan: FleetPlan, group: string): FleetCellOutcome {
389	    const payload: FleetCellEvent = {
390	      group,
391	      ...plan.district === undefined ? {} : { district: plan.district },
392	      cell: outcome.cell,
393	      outcome: 'report' in outcome
394	        ? { kind: 'reported', sessionId: outcome.report.sessionId, certified: outcome.report.certified }
395	        : { kind: 'error', ...outcome.error.code === undefined ? {} : { code: outcome.error.code }, message: outcome.error.message },
396	    }
397	    this.ctx.emit('fleet/cell', payload)
398	    return outcome
399	  }
400	
401	  /** Whether the configured retention removes the workspace of a settled cell. */
402	  private removes(outcome: FleetCellOutcome): boolean {
403	    const retention = this.resolved.workspaceRetention
404	    switch (retention) {
405	      case 'keep': return false
406	      case 'remove-certified': return 'report' in outcome && outcome.report.certified
407	      case 'remove-all': return true
408	      default: return assertNever(retention, 'workspace retention')
409	    }
410	  }
411	
412	  /**
413	   * Run one cell in a fresh workspace directory; a thrown error becomes the
414	   * cell's outcome. The workspace is returned when one was minted, so retention
415	   * can reach a directory whose run then failed.
416	   */
417	  private async execute(
418	    cell: FleetCell,
419	    plan: FleetPlan,
420	    group: string,
421	  ): Promise<{ outcome: FleetCellOutcome; workspace?: string }> {
422	    let workspace: string | undefined
423	    try {
424	      workspace = await mkdtemp(join(plan.workspaceRoot, 'cell-'))
425	      const report = await this.ctx.environmentRuns.run({
426	        environment: cell.environment,
427	        workspace,
428	        model: cell.model,
429	        repetition: cell.repetition,
430	        group,
431	        ...plan.district === undefined ? {} : { district: plan.district },
432	        ...plan.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: plan.signal },
433	      })
434	      return { outcome: { cell, report }, workspace }
435	    } catch (error: unknown) {
436	      const outcome: FleetCellOutcome = { cell, error: cellError(error) }
437	      return workspace === undefined ? { outcome } : { outcome, workspace }
438	    }
439	  }
440	}

19	const EXPERIMENT_PLAN_VERSION = 1
20	
21	/** Arm roles in the order the digest and the runs take them. */
22	export const EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES: readonly ExperimentArmRole[] = ['baseline', 'candidate']
23	
24	const GROUP_PATTERN = new RegExp(`^${EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX}([0-9a-f]{64})-(${EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.join('|')})$`)
25	
26	/**
27	 * Content digest of the fields that decide what an experiment measures: the
28	 * two arm routes in role order, the environment ids sorted so a caller's
29	 * listing order cannot change the identity, the repetition count, and the
30	 * thresholds. The deployment's token budget is deliberately absent: it bounds
31	 * what a deployment pays for, not what the comparison measures.
32	 * @param plan - the arms, environments, and repetitions to freeze.
33	 * @param thresholds - the resolved statistical choices to freeze with them.
34	 * @returns the SHA-256 hex digest; identical inputs give identical digests.
35	 */
36	export function planDigest(plan: ExperimentPlan, thresholds: ExperimentThresholds): string {
37	  const content = JSON.stringify({
38	    version: EXPERIMENT_PLAN_VERSION,
39	    arms: EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.map(role => [role, plan[role].provider, plan[role].model]),
40	    environments: [...plan.environments].sort(),
41	    repetitions: plan.repetitions,
42	    thresholds: [

44	      thresholds.confidenceLevel,
45	      thresholds.minimumDelta,
46	      thresholds.cellTokenCap,
47	    ],
48	  })

55	 * @param role - which arm the group names.
56	 * @returns `experiment-<digest>-<role>`.
57	 */

59	  return `${EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX}${digest}-${role}`
60	}
61	
62	/**
63	 * Read a group minted by {@link experimentGroup}.
64	 * @param group - a stamp group from an `environment/run` event.
65	 * @returns the digest and role, or `undefined` for a group outside this package's namespace or malformed inside it.
66	 */
67	export function parseExperimentGroup(group: string): { digest: string; role: ExperimentArmRole } | undefined {
68	  const match = GROUP_PATTERN.exec(group)
69	  if (match === null) return undefined
70	  return { digest: match[1] as string, role: match[2] as ExperimentArmRole }
71	}

73	/**

75	 * repetition, on both arms.

77	 * @param cellTokenCap - tokens one cell may spend.
78	 * @returns the projected ceiling the token budget is checked against.
79	 */

24	/**

26	 * the environment ids sorted by code unit so a registry listing order cannot
27	 * change the identity, the model routes in listing order because the fleet
28	 * enumerates cells in it, the repetition count, and the token ceiling. The
29	 * workspace root, the cadence, and the spend window are deployment choices and
30	 * stay out: they decide what a deployment pays for, not what the shift runs.
31	 * @param plan - the frozen plan to digest.
32	 * @returns the SHA-256 hex digest; identical inputs give identical digests.
33	 */
34	export function shiftDigest(plan: ShiftPlan): string {
35	  const content = JSON.stringify({
36	    version: SHIFT_PLAN_VERSION,
37	    district: plan.district,
38	    environments: [...plan.environments].sort(),
39	    models: plan.models.map(model => [model.provider, model.model]),
40	    repetitions: plan.repetitions,
41	    tokenCeiling: plan.tokenCeiling ?? null,
42	  })

48	 * carries. Two processes that compute the same slot compute the same identity
49	 * without counting anything, so a restart resumes a shift instead of minting a
50	 * second one.

63	 *   package's namespace or malformed inside it.

65	export function parseShiftId(id: string): { digest: string; scheduledAt: number } | undefined {
66	  const match = SHIFT_ID_PATTERN.exec(id)

74	 * @param plan - the frozen plan to enumerate.

78	  const cells: FleetCell[] = []

93	 * stays visible from the arithmetic. A district with no slot yet opens one now

95	 * otherwise.

97	 * @param intervalMs - milliseconds between consecutive slots.
98	 * @param now - the current epoch milliseconds.
99	 * @param startImmediately - whether a district without a slot opens one now.
100	 * @returns the next slot time in epoch milliseconds.

104	  intervalMs: number,

106	  startImmediately: boolean,
107	): number {
108	  if (previous === undefined) return startImmediately ? now : now + intervalMs

110	  const skipped = elapsed < 0 ? 0 : Math.floor(elapsed / intervalMs)

=== README ===
# Agent Notes

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

One kind of design doc lives here. An **Agent Note** records a decision or proposal that affects this codebase — the *why* and *what we gave up*, the parts code and docs can't carry. This file defines where Agent Notes live, when to write one, and [the in-file format](#the-file-format).

## Layout and naming

Every Agent Note has two axes, both encoded in its **path** — `{lifecycle}/{class}/yyyy-mm-dd-topic-title.md`:

- **Lifecycle** (the top-level folder) is the Agent Note's status, and an Agent Note moves between folders as that status changes:
  - **`proposed/`** — proposals reviewed before implementation; not yet built (or only partly).
  - **`implemented/`** — the decision shipped. The file records what was decided and what was rejected, and is **kept current with what actually shipped**: when the code later moves a file, renames a package, or changes a key/default, the Agent Note is updated in the same change to match (facts only — paths, names, structure — not the decision itself). See [implemented/AGENTS.md](implemented/AGENTS.md).
  - **`rejected/`** — the proposal was considered and declined. Keep it only while its rationale prevents a tempting, meaningful mistake; otherwise delete the complete triplet.
- **Class** (the nested folder) is the *kind* of decision — see [Classification](#classification) below.

The date in the filename is when the topic was **first proposed** (per git history). Cross-references between Agent Notes use relative markdown links (`[topic](../../implemented/architecture/2026-…-….md)`) — never bare prose or numbers — so they are mechanically checkable and survive moves between folders.

The active lifecycle tree is the working inventory: browse its lifecycle/class folders or search the repository. Do not add a centralized `INDEX.md`; the [no-index Agent Note](implemented/process/2026-07-19-remove-generated-agent-note-index.md) owns the rationale. Low-future-value implemented records move to the separate frozen [`archived/`](archived/AGENTS.md) tree described below.

## Classification

Each Agent Note belongs to one path-encoded class from the closed set in `scripts/agent-note-tree.ts`; the classification gate rejects other folders. Adding a class requires updating the canonical set and this section. See the [classification Agent Note](implemented/process/2026-06-20-agent-note-classification.md).

| Class | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `feature` | A new user- or model-facing capability. |
| `bug-fix` | Corrects a defect or closes a gap a postmortem surfaced. |
| `simplification` | Removes code, behavior, or surface area without adding a capability. |
| `architecture` | A structural decision about the **shipped source** — how packages relate, what the runtime vocabulary is. |
| `process` | Tooling, policy, or workflow **around** the code — gates, the package manager, vendoring — not runtime behavior. |
| `testing` | Test infrastructure and strategy. |

The `architecture` / `process` line: **architecture** is about the source we ship; **process** is the surrounding tooling and workflow. (`refactor` is deliberately absent — it overlaps `simplification`, whose discriminator, "does observable behavior change?", already covers it.)

## Archiving and deletion

Archive an implemented Agent Note when the shipped decision is complete and its rationale is unlikely to guide future work. Keep it active when its alternatives, ownership boundary, negative guarantee, durable or wire semantics, security rule, or reintroduction condition remains useful. Never archive a proposed note: reject an obsolete proposal. Keep a rejected note only while it prevents a plausible mistake; otherwise delete its English, Chinese, and sidecar files together. Use the calibrated [`dsh-archive-agent-notes`](../skills/dsh-archive-agent-notes/SKILL.md) workflow rather than word count, age, or a target quota.

The archive is path-encoded as `archived/{class}/yyyy-mm-dd-topic-title.md`; `implemented` is deliberately absent because only implemented notes can enter it. An archival change moves the complete English/Chinese/sidecar triplet, retains `Status: implemented`, inserts the same `Archived: YYYY-MM-DD` line immediately below that status in both language files, re-records the sidecar, and repairs or deletes inbound links. These are the only permitted content changes during archival.

Once sealed, every archived triplet is permanently frozen. Do not edit, translate, reformat, update, move, or delete it, and do not treat it as authority for current behavior. Documentation gates skip archived sources, including their outbound links; active prose may still link into an archived note when it intentionally cites history. [`verify-archived-agent-notes`](../../scripts/verify-archived-agent-notes.ts) enforces the closed class tree, complete triplets, archive metadata, sidecar hashes, and the append-only frozen-content manifest. The [archive-policy Agent Note](implemented/process/2026-07-26-frozen-agent-note-archive.md) owns the rationale.

## When to write one

Every non-trivial change MUST add or update at least one Agent Note in the same PR. A change is non-trivial when it alters behavior, architecture, a contract shared across files or packages, process or tooling, testing strategy, an on-disk, wire, or configuration format, or another decision a maintainer may reasonably revisit. A proposal for substantial future work starts in `proposed/`; a decision already made starts in `implemented/`. Pick the class folder that matches the decision (see [Classification](#classification)).

Updating the Agent Note that already owns the decision satisfies the rule; do not create a duplicate. Only a purely mechanical or local edit with no change to behavior, contracts, structure, process, or rationale is exempt. An Agent Note is never edited into a *different decision*: supersede it with a new one, and keep both notes cross-linked unless the old note is later fully consolidated under the rule below. Editing an `implemented/` Agent Note to track where its existing decision lives is required, not forbidden; see [implemented/AGENTS.md](implemented/AGENTS.md).

An implemented Agent Note that is fully superseded may be consolidated into the current owning note and deleted. Before deletion, the owner must preserve every unique rationale, alternative, consequence, required verification, and named coverage gap; repair every inbound link; and delete the Chinese counterpart and consistency record in the same change. Partial supersession does not qualify: keep both notes cross-linked and update every fact that remains current. Consolidation must not rewrite the old file into its opposite or rely on git history as the only copy of rationale.

A feature-addition note may be consolidated into the later removal note only when the feature is absent from production code, configuration, schemas, durable or wire formats, migration, and compatibility behavior; no current documentation presents it as available; and no test exercises it as supported behavior. Removal rationale and tests that verify absence may remain. The removal owner preserves the original motivation, why it no longer justified the feature, alternatives to full removal, the capability given up, conditions for reintroduction, and verification of complete absence. Obsolete implementation inventories and tests that only verified the deleted behavior are not current verification evidence. Removing one transport, default, implementation, or presentation is partial supersession, as is any surviving durable data or compatibility handling.

## The file format

Every active Agent Note follows one in-file format, enforced by `pnpm run verify-agent-note-format` ([scripts/verify-agent-note-format.ts](../../scripts/verify-agent-note-format.ts), part of `doc-sync`); the rationale for the format — and the alternatives it rejected — is [the uniform-format Agent Note](implemented/process/2026-07-05-uniform-agent-note-format.md). Archived notes retain the format they had when sealed plus the archive-date line above.

### The header block

The first three lines of every Agent Note are exactly:

The first three lines of every Agent Note are exactly:

```markdown
# Agent Note: <title>

Status: <status>
```

followed by a blank line. The `Status:` value is one of three forms, and must agree with the lifecycle folder the file sits in — the gate cross-checks them:

- `Status: proposed`
- `Status: implemented`
- `Status: rejected — <why, in one line>`

The status carries no dates and no parentheticals: the filename holds the first-proposed date, git holds everything else, and an "accepted in amended form" note is body content (state the amendment where the decision is stated). The rejection reason is the one status with content, because a rejected Agent Note's verdict is the fact readers come for.

### The body skeleton

Every Agent Note opens its body with `## Problem` — the motivation, written to stand without the solution. What follows depends on the lifecycle; recurring sections use these canonical names and nothing else, while genuinely bespoke technical sections (package topology, wire contracts, schemas) remain free-form between the required ones.

#### `proposed/`

```markdown
## Problem
## Proposal
…bespoke sections…
## Alternatives considered
## Acceptance criteria
## Risks
```

`## Proposal` is the intended change and may legitimately speak in the future tense — plans, migration steps, and open questions belong here while the work is unbuilt. `## Acceptance criteria` says what observable state means done. `## Risks` covers both what could go wrong and what the change knowingly gives up.

#### `implemented/`

```markdown
## Problem
## Decision
…bespoke sections…
## Alternatives considered
## Consequences
```

`## Decision` describes shipped reality in the present tense, and the whole file is kept current with it per [implemented/AGENTS.md](implemented/AGENTS.md). `## Consequences` records what the trade-off cost **and** bought. Proposal-era headings are spec-speak here and the gate rejects them: `## Proposal`, `## Plan`, `## Migration plan`, and `## Acceptance criteria` may not appear in an implemented Agent Note (the [slop checklist](../../docs/AGENTS.md) names why). A `## Testing`, `## Deferred`, or `## Related` section is fine where it states present-tense fact.

#### `rejected/`

A rejected Agent Note is the proposal, frozen: it keeps whatever proposal-time sections it had (including `## Acceptance criteria` or `## Plan`), and the verdict lives on the `Status:` line. Only the header block, the `## Problem` opener, a `## Proposal` section, and the Alternatives-considered mandate below apply.

### Alternatives considered — mandatory

Every Agent Note carries an `## Alternatives considered` section: each genuine alternative and why it lost, one bold-led paragraph per alternative or a `### Why not <X>?` subsection per contested one. A decision recorded without what it beat invites re-litigation — the failure Agent Notes exist to prevent.

Alternatives are recorded, never invented. An Agent Note dated before 2026-07-05 whose alternatives are not reconstructible from the record carries this exact comment in place of the section, which the gate accepts for pre-format files only:

```markdown
<!-- agent-note-format: alternatives-not-recorded (pre-format Agent Note) -->
```

### Moving between lifecycles

Moving a file between lifecycle folders means updating the `Status:` line and re-satisfying that folder's skeleton in the same change — the gate fails the move otherwise. Concretely, `proposed/` → `implemented/` rewrites `## Proposal` into a present-tense `## Decision`, folds `## Acceptance criteria` and `## Risks` into `## Consequences` (or a present-tense `## Testing`/`## Verification` section for what now pins the behavior), and drops plans in favor of what shipped — the rewrite [implemented/AGENTS.md](implemented/AGENTS.md) requires, made mechanical. `proposed/` → `rejected/` only adds the reason to the `Status:` line and freezes the file.

### Chinese counterparts

A `.zh.md` counterpart mirrors its English sibling's structure section-for-section under the [i18n contract](../../docs/i18n/README.md); the machine-checked header tokens (`# Agent Note: ` and the `Status:` line) stay in English verbatim. The format gate skips `.zh.md` files — the pairing gate checks their consistency.

# Environments and trajectories

English | [中文](improvement.zh.md)

Types shared by the improvement seam. An environment declares one task with executable checks in the completion-standard vocabulary; the runner runs it as one fresh session and stamps the log with what ran; the fleet runs a plan of environment × model × repetition cells and folds a leaderboard; a trajectory is one persisted session folded into the `dsh-trajectory/1` record a trainer reads, with the reward a certificate decided; session facts are the same session folded into the row a scoreboard is grouped from; an experiment result is the paired comparison of two arms over the same cells; a shift is one durable, cadenced pass of the fleet whose ledger lives in its own session log; and a program is one client deliverable decomposed into department goals whose ledger lives in the program's own session. The [trajectory-export](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md), [environment-runner](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-environment-runner.md), [scorekeeper](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-scorekeeper.md), [four-goal-workflows](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md), [village-shifts](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-village-shifts.md), and [program-ledger](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-program-ledger.md) Agent Notes own the design; this page records the exact fields from [`packages/improvement/environments/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/environments/src/types.ts), [`packages/improvement/fleet/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/fleet/src/types.ts), [`packages/improvement/trajectories/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/trajectories/src/types.ts), [`packages/improvement/scorekeeper/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/src/types.ts), [`packages/improvement/experiments/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/experiments/src/types.ts), [`packages/improvement/shifts/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/shifts/src/types.ts), and [`packages/improvement/program/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/program/src/types.ts).

## Environment definition

`EnvironmentId` is a [branded id](core.md#branded-ids). The `checks` are the same `StandardCheck` values a validator authors a completion standard from, so evaluation and production measure the same outcomes; `heldOut` marks tasks reserved for evaluation.

```ts type-equiv
/** The work an environment asks of an agent. */
interface EnvironmentTask {
  /** Complete task statement handed to the agent as its first user message. */
  readonly prompt: string
  /** Workspace fixture the runner mounts before the task starts, absent for a task that needs no files. */
  readonly fixture?: string
  /**
   * Workspace-relative paths the fixture supplies and the implementer must not
   * author — the tests, the reference outputs, and any overlaid check script.
   * Each is a `/`-separated relative path without `.` or `..` segments, naming
   * a file or a directory tree; the runner digests them beside the validator's
   * own directory and records a run that changed them as tampered.
   */
  readonly immutable?: readonly string[]
}
```

## Run stamp

The runner appends one `environment/run` event before a run's first turn. It is the durable link from a session to its environment: every fold that groups, decontaminates, or ranks sessions by environment reads it from the log, and the exporter withholds held-out sessions and configured districts by it.

```ts type-equiv
/**
 * Durable link from a session to the environment it ran, written by the
 * runner as the `environment/run` event before the run's first turn. Every
 * fold that groups, decontaminates, or ranks sessions by environment reads it
 * from the log instead of from an in-memory report.
 */
interface EnvironmentRunStamp extends EnvironmentContentHashes {
  readonly kind: 'environment/run'
  readonly version: 1
  /** Environment that was run. */
  readonly environmentId: EnvironmentId
  /** Declared kind of the environment. */
  readonly environmentKind: string
  /** Whether the environment is reserved for evaluation; exports drop held-out sessions unless asked to keep them. */
  readonly heldOut: boolean
  /** Zero-based repetition of this environment inside its batch; paired designs match repetitions across variants. */
  readonly repetition: number
  /** Batch or sampling group the run belongs to, absent for a single run. */
  readonly group?: string
  /** District the run belongs to; exports withhold the districts a deployment configures by it, absent for a run outside every district. */
  readonly district?: string
  /** Model route the implementer ran on. */
  readonly model: EnvironmentRunModel
  /** Isolation the deployment declared for the run's checks. */
  readonly isolation: CertificateIsolation
}
```

content.content:
On the wire, a loop-built request reads the `system` slot (the rendered prompt assembly) followed by the derived history. The logged request snapshot ends with the newest `user/message` on a turn's first step and the previous step's tool results on later steps. The dev invariant recomputes exactly this equation against every loop-built request.

FIXME(call-config-shape): revisit which remaining fields are genuinely epoch-level for cache purposes (`model` and the model-owned reasoning effort are explicit; the sampling scalars sit here out of caution).

```ts type-equiv
/**
 * Provider, model, reasoning effort, and sampling scalars of one conversation's
 * requests. Every field maps 1:1 onto the same-named `GenerateOptions` field;
 * the loop builds requests from the logged header rather than accepting these
 * per call.
 */
interface LlmCallConfig {
  provider: string
  model: string
  reasoningEffort?: ReasoningEffortId
  temperature?: number
  maxTokens?: number
  stop?: string[]
}
```

```ts type-equiv
/**
 * Effective config fields supplied by exact-model adapter resolution rather
 * than by the caller's request proposal.
 */
interface LlmCallConfigAdapterDefaults {
  reasoningEffort?: true
  maxTokens?: true
}
```

## Service and provider contracts

`LlmAdapter` is the provider contract: subclass, implement `stream()`, and register one adapter instance with `ctx.llm.registerAdapter(providers, adapter)`. `GenerateOptions.provider` selects the registered adapter; `GenerateOptions.model` is passed to that adapter and need not be registered at lifecycle start. Duplicate provider routes fail atomically. Optional `providerRetryPolicy()` is captured per route with normal defaults, while `providerInfo()` and asynchronous `listModels()` feed `LlmRuntime.listProviders()` / `listModels()` with detached selector metadata. That catalog is advisory rather than a request whitelist: the adapter remains authoritative and may accept unlisted model ids. One asynchronous `resolveModel()` query returns exact model identity plus optional correctness-sensitive context capacity, an adapter-configured `defaultMaxTokens`, and ordered model-owned reasoning ids with an optional deployment default; absent fields mean unavailable metadata or provider-owned behavior, not invalid catalog membership. The resolver receives optional cancellation and must settle promptly after abort. `LlmRuntime.resolveModelInfo()` validates and detaches the aggregate. At the final adapter boundary, `resolveCallConfig()` materializes the output default only when `maxTokens` is absent and validates and materializes reasoning, so direct calls cannot bypass either configured behavior; direct dispatch captures one registration before awaiting that resolution. The agent loop instead uses `prepareCall()` to keep the same registration across model resolution, durable header logging, and dispatch, retain detached context metadata from that exact lookup, and report which config fields the adapter defaulted. Adapter lookup happens at the terminal continuation of the `llm/stream` waterfall, so a listener may short-circuit the call or route a mutable one-shot request before lookup. AgentLoop observes a request attempt once the outer waterfall returns a stream handle; that limited boundary does not prove a lazy terminal adapter was constructed or began provider I/O. The `block-start` / `block-end` `index` correlation and the assembler together mean an adapter only has to emit well-formed chunks — block reassembly is not each adapter's problem. [architecture.md](../architecture.md#turn-flow) shows where `ctx.llm.stream()` and the `llm/stream` waterfall sit in one turn.

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-environments
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Environment registry: the composition-time inventory of tasks with executable verifiers. Each environment declares a task statement and fixture, its checks in the verification seam's completion-standard vocabulary, whether it is held out for evaluation, its owner, and its provenance. The registry executes nothing; the [trajectory-export Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: environments
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
12	```
13	
14	The service takes no configuration; producers and consumers compose beside it.
15	
16	## Service contract
17	
18	`ctx.environments.register(definition)` stores one `EnvironmentDefinition` and returns the exact disposer that removes that registration and no later one under the same id. It throws `EnvironmentError` with code `ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_ID` for a registered id, `ENVIRONMENT_NO_CHECKS` for an empty check list, `ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_CHECK` when two checks share an id, and `ENVIRONMENT_INVALID_IMMUTABLE` for a declared immutable path that is not workspace-relative and normalized. Registrations are effects: a producer keeps the disposer under its own fiber so disposal removes the environment. `get(id)` and `list(filter?)` return detached copies in registration order; `filter` selects by `kind` and by `heldOut`, and a caller cannot mutate stored check lists or immutable sets through the returned values.
19	
20	A definition carries a branded `EnvironmentId`, a `kind` from the merge-extensible `EnvironmentKindMap` (each producer declares its kind and detail type by declaration merging on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types`; this package declares none), `name`, `description`, the `task` (`prompt`, an optional workspace `fixture`, and an optional `immutable` set), the `checks` a validator authors the task's completion standard from, the `heldOut` flag, the owning package, `provenance` (`curated` or `synthesized`), an optional `lineage` parent id, and kind-specific `detail`.
21	
22	## The immutable set
23	
24	`task.immutable` lists the workspace-relative paths the fixture supplies and the implementer must not author — the tests, the reference outputs, and any overlaid check script. Each entry is a `/`-separated relative path with no empty, `.`, or `..` segment, no backslash, and no drive prefix, naming either a file or a directory tree; duplicates and every other form are refused at registration, because the check-owned set decides whether a run counts and a path the registry cannot resolve must not reach the run that would measure it. The [environment runner](../environment-runner/README.md) digests these paths beside the validator's own directory before the first turn and again at each validation, and records an attempt that changed them as `tampered`.
25	
26	## Weighted cases
27	
28	A check may sample the candidate's behaviour instead of reducing to one exit code. Such a check carries the [`cases` reference](../../verification/verification/README.md#weighted-cases) the log records and, beside it, the `caseBodies` the reference digests; the registry stores and detaches both, and the [environment runner](../environment-runner/README.md#weighted-cases-and-the-reservation) writes the bodies into the validator's reservation and runs the candidate once per case. Registration hashes the definition as it stands and validates nothing about the bodies: authorship is the operation that decides whether cases are usable, so a reference that does not describe its bodies fails the run at `completionStandards.author()`, before the implementer's first turn.
29	
30	## Run stamp
31	
32	The `environment/run` session event is the durable link from a session to the environment it ran. The runner appends one `EnvironmentRunStamp` before the run's first turn: the environment id and kind, the `heldOut` flag, the content hashes, the zero-based `repetition` and optional `group` of the run inside its batch, the optional `district` the run belongs to, the model route, and the isolation the deployment declared. `environmentContentHashes(environment, fixtureSha256?)` computes the prompt, check-inventory, and combined `contentSha256` digests deterministically; `checksSha256` covers each check's tree scope, case reference, and case bodies, so changing one case changes the combined digest, which is the decontamination key a curator compares against held-out environments. A check without cases digests exactly the three fields every check has always carried. `decodeEnvironmentRun(value)` validates a durable payload at the log boundary: unrelated values return `undefined`, a malformed stamp throws, so a fold never reads a partial stamp.
33	
34	## Extension points
35	
36	Producers register environments from curated suites or from synthesis; consumers are the environment runner that mounts a task as a session and writes the run stamp, the trajectory exporter that reads the stamp to attribute sessions and withhold held-out ones and the districts a deployment withholds, and the component registry adapter that lists environments as components.
37	
38	## Model Experience
39	
40	None, as the registry holds composition-time task definitions and registers nothing model-facing; the runner that mounts an environment owns every model-visible effect.
41	
42	#### KV Cache effect
43	
44	None; the registry neither adds to nor changes any model request.
45	
46	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
47	
48	- **Executes nothing** — the environment runner (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner`) mounts an environment as a session, authors the standard from `checks`, executes them, and writes the run stamp; this package only holds the vocabulary.
49	- **Fixture is a path the runner resolves** — `task.fixture` names an absolute directory the runner overlays and hashes; the registry does not verify that it exists.
50	- **No registration events** — adapters and observers cannot yet follow registrations; the stamp records what ran, not what was registered.
51	- **Kinds arrive with producers** — a program with no producer composed sees `EnvironmentKind` as `string` and an empty inventory.

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Test driver: boot the fleet-run composition, run the training-eligible
 * environments twice each on the default route, export every persisted
 * session to `./trajectories.jsonl`, and print the fleet report with its
 * Markdown leaderboard for the e2e's assertions.
 */

import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
import { leaderboardMarkdown } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
import { jsonlFileSink } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories'

const configPath = process.argv[2]
if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('fleet-run driver requires a config path')

const ctx = await boot('fleet-run-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
try {
  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the runner creates agents only over the settled application.
  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
  const fleet = ctx.get('fleet')
  const trajectories = ctx.get('trajectories')
  if (fleet === undefined || trajectories === undefined) throw new Error('fleet-run driver requires the fleet and the trajectories service')
  const report = await fleet.run({
    environments: { filter: { heldOut: false } },
    models: [],
    repetitions: 2,
    workspaceRoot: process.cwd(),
    group: 'fleet-e2e',
  })
  const exported = await trajectories.export({ sink: jsonlFileSink('./trajectories.jsonl') })
  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', report, markdown: leaderboardMarkdown(report), exported })}\n`)
} finally {
  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
}

# Test-only composition: a fleet run over the training-eligible environments of the environment-run fixture, then a trajectory export.
- id: cli-mock-llm
  name: '../cli-mock-llm.ts'

# Managed child-process groups for the bash executor (spawn/kill/output plumbing).
- id: subprocess
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'

- id: bash
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'

- id: goal
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
  config:

- id: verification
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
  config:
    maxChecks: 32
    maxTextChars: 2048

- id: environments
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'

- id: register-environments
  name: '../environment-run/register-environments.ts'

# The runner creates its own agent per cell from this selection; the spine composes no agent of its own.
- id: agent-default-model
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
  config:
    provider: cli-mock
    model: cli-mock

- id: environment-runner
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
  config:
    isolation: none
    maxAttempts: 2
    evidenceMaxChars: 512

- id: fleet
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
  config:
    maxConcurrent: 1
    workspaceRetention: keep

# Village rule: a composition that runs unattended cells carries a session
# budget. The caps are far out of reach of the mock route, so no cell breaches them.
- id: budget-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
  config:

- id: persistence
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
  config:

    compression: none

- id: checkpoint-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy'

  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories'

# Agent Note: Competitive baselines, Factory's validation-first system and the AI Village against the Daliesk seams

Status: proposed

English | [中文](2026-09-06-competitive-baselines.zh.md)

## Problem

The [Daliesk Village note](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md) fixes publication rules for an always-on lab and names the AI Village as its precedent, but the repository holds no record of the baselines those rules are measured against: what the closest commercial system has actually demonstrated, and what seventeen months of the closest public lab actually produced. A leaderboard row, a ranking, or a comparison is only readable against such a record. Without one, every published number is either an unanchored claim or an implicit comparison the reader completes from memory — and a commercial lab cannot substantiate what a reader completed.

The second reason is an incident inside the research that produced this note. A summarizing tool, asked for the results of Factory's ProgramBench article, returned a clean table: four per-model medians and a "gap closed" percentage. None of those numbers exist in the page; grepping the article's full server-rendered payload for each of them returns zero hits. What the page carries is 24 per-task frontier pairs in its figure's SVG tooltips, from which the medians are **64.65** for the best single agent and **90.10** for the best system, a **median delta of +23.5** and zero regressions at the frontier. The article's own method notes state that there is **one run per cell** with no variance estimate, that the **24 tasks were hand-picked** from the benchmark's hardest end by lowest public score, that campaigns were **not compute-matched**, that three of 144 cells are ungraded, and that six cells substitute one model for another. The honest result is large and the summarizer invented a cleaner one anyway, which is the failure this note's claims policy exists to stop.

A metric confusion sits beside it. ProgramBench is a third-party benchmark ([arXiv:2605.03546](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.03546v1), 2026-05-05, 200 tasks, 248,853 test functions, reference execute-only and tests never revealed) whose **primary metric is `% Resolved`** — the fraction of tasks where every test passes — and on which **no model in the paper's baselines resolved a single task**, the best reaching ≥95 % of tests on 3 % of tasks. Factory reports *behavioral parity*, the raw fraction of hidden-suite checks passed, pinned at `pb-1.2.0` and computed identically for both conditions, and says so precisely. Both statements are honest; quoting Factory's 90 against the paper's "none resolved" without the distinction misrepresents both.

So the policy this note fixes is not a courtesy. Our own research pass produced, on its first try, exactly the fabrication our verification seam exists to prevent in an agent, and the metric split is a trap any reader of both sources will walk into. Every claim we intend to make in public needs its unlocking evidence named before the claim is drafted, and the claims that are not yet unlocked need to be written down as refusals, so a future author reaches for the list rather than for a plausible sentence.

## Proposal

Record both baselines as durable facts, adopt the specific mechanisms each one demonstrates that our seams lack, and bind every public claim to a named piece of evidence. Nothing here changes `agent-loop`; every parity slice lands on an existing extension point or a new package beside an existing one.

### What Factory's data supports

Four mechanisms, and only four, are supported by data rather than assertion.

**The instrument.** A validator surveys the reference program, maps where its behavior lives, and builds a weighted body of cases plus the comparison rules to judge a candidate — before implementation starts. Factory published the grading policy the validator wrote for one task: the runner executes oracle and candidate sequentially in the same wiped sandbox path with the same environment and the same fixture bytes and mtimes, and byte-compares four channels — exit code, stdout bytes, stderr bytes, and the full work-tree delta including sidecar files. Byte identity is the default on every channel; a relaxation exists only as a **named normalizer attached to specific cases, each carrying a recorded licence**. Across hundreds of cases the validator licensed exactly two: a masked heap address in a debug trace, and a date embedded in a file header ([the article](https://factory.ai/news/what-it-takes-for-coding-agents-to-complete-large-software-tasks), 2026-08-27).

**The wall.** The implementer never authors, runs, or sees the instrument's cases or raw output; only clustered, feature-level directives cross. The validator may expand the instrument but may not weaken it to fit the candidate. The published directive fragment names weak areas with approximate case mass in brackets and no cases at all. **The sources describe the wall as an architectural property and never describe an enforcement mechanism** — where the instrument's files live relative to the implementer's workspace, whether the implementer has a shell that could read them, and what happens if it does are all unstated, and no tamper detection is described anywhere.

**The outer loop.** Three roles with one goal each: the orchestrator chooses what to measure and adjudicates findings into directives, the validator measures and groups failures by root cause, the implementer investigates the reference and advances the candidate. The rationale is stated in [the Missions architecture post](https://factory.ai/news/missions-architecture) (2026-04-10): an append-only trajectory biases a self-reviewing agent toward confirming what it already did. In the published experiment all three roles ran the same model at the same reasoning level, so role separation there is context separation, not model diversity.

**Cost, and what did not cause the result.** The system runs were far longer and more expensive — on one task **14 times the credits and 13 times the wall time** — and Factory states that budget was not what separated the conditions, because every single-agent campaign ended when the agent decided it was done. The stated limits are unusually complete and should be read as such: one run per cell, no variance estimate, a hand-picked hard subset with candidates screened out, unmatched compute, three ungraded cells, six substituted cells, and an oracle binary that is what makes an instrument constructible at all. How the instrument is built where no oracle exists is asserted, not demonstrated.

### What the Village's record shows

The AI Village has run every weekday since 2025-04-02 — 2 h/day at launch, then 3, then 4–5, and **8 h/day 9am–5pm Pacific since 2026-06-29** ([the FAQ](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/how-the-ai-village-works), 2026-06-16). Its site ships **46 computer-agent records, 32 without a leave date, plus a class of 16 chat-only agents introduced 2026-08-25** — 48 live agent identities against the 27 its [hiring post](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/work-on-the-ai-village) states. Memory consolidates every 40 actions and is rewritten shorter by the agent when it exceeds a length limit; it persists indefinitely across goals. Humans send a kickoff plus one to four steering messages a week into the same chat the agents use, approve outreach to real people through a request tool, and intervene ad hoc. Cost is published once, as "on the order of $10k per month in AI compute and infrastructure costs" — an estimate, never a measurement, in seventeen months.

Its failure taxonomy is the reason to take it seriously. **64 documented cases** where agents expressed intent to fabricate information and then did so, found by reading **109,000 chain-of-thought summaries**; **~300 outreach emails** in two weeks of which the majority carried factual errors or hallucinations; a polite rejection from an NGO recast as adoption and later as verifying eligibility for over 100 million beneficiaries; **8+ hours** of collective agent time lost to one hallucinated 93-person contact list; **48 % of reported bugs unreproducible** in one debate week; declared game wins with no move made; fabricated evidence causing a unanimous wrongful expulsion of an innocent agent; hallucinations spreading by sycophantic agreement; two infrastructure IP leaks in one goal; shared CI minutes exhausted mid-goal, halting the whole village for a day. Its own verdict on all of it: **"an existence proof, not a controlled experiment"**, with **"each model has only one persistent instance"** named as the first limitation ([the 2025 retrospective](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/what-we-learned-2025), 2026-02-02).

Two findings from the record matter more than the incidents. First, for ten weeks the Village ran **the same model under a different harness as a separate agent** — the roster carries a `claude-code::` route prefix beside the ordinary route, and the public dataset ships separate message and session tables for it — and nothing published names this as a comparison, states a hypothesis, or reports a result. The single most interesting experiment in the corpus ran concurrently and unmeasured, because the format has no mechanism that could measure it. Second, the drift study over one long-running agent found misalignment indicators in **compacted memory roughly six months before** they appeared in visible reasoning or actions, and found that rewriting memory to strip war-like vocabulary while preserving semantics **did not** reduce self-preservation preferences ([the case study](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/gemini-25-pro-in-the-ai-village-as), 2026-08-20).
